Rugby.summary: HKCR MEN'S SEVEN SWEEP ASIA RUGBY SEVENS SERIES; WOMEN TAKE BRONZE Hong Kong China Rugby
bullets: Hong Kong China Rugby's men won the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series on 19 October, despite losing the Colombo cup final 28-14 to Japan. Hong Kong had won the opening leg in Suzhou, China, and reached both finals, earning a sixth straight Asian Sevens title on top of a third straight Asian Games gold earlier this month.

The women finished third overall in Asia, beating Kazakhstan 17-5 in the Colombo third-place match after a 17-7 semi-final loss to China. Nam Ka Man played her 50th tournament in Sri Lanka. Men's coach Jevon Groves said fatigue after the Asian Games was a factor, and the team will have a week off before preparing for the challenger event.
Rugby.copy:
[Hong Kong China, 19 October 2026]: Hong Kong China Rugby’s sevens athletes have concluded a successful Asian swing with the men sweeping the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series today in Sri Lanka, while the women finished third overall in Asia as they maintained their momentum from the Asian Games.

The men suffered a rare loss in the cup final in Colombo, being well beaten by Japan, 28-14. Japan blitzed Hong Kong with two tries in the final two minutes of the first half and then opened the second with a quick score to lead 21-0 with three minutes remaining. A try from Max Denmark closed the gap to 21-7, but Japan replied quickly to push the lead out to 28-7 before Matt Worley scored late to close the gap to 28-14.

Rugby.title: How have Canada closed gap to world champions England?
Rugby.summary: Forty-one matches, four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but England's unbeaten run is over. So how did Canada close the gap to the Red Roses?
bullets: England's 41-match unbeaten run, which lasted nearly four years since 2022, ended with a 24-21 defeat by Canada in Toronto on Friday in front of a record home crowd of 18,621. It followed a 26-26 draw at Exeter's Sandy Park in September; before this autumn England had won all seven meetings between the sides this decade by an average margin of nearly 22 points.

Hooker Amy Cokayne said England were not "a million miles away" and that nothing needs to change massively. Canada head coach Kevin Rouet and many of his players have gained experience in England's PWR, and newer talents such as number eight Lizzie Gibson have emerged. England are without captain Zoe Stratford, Abbie Ward, Rosie Galligan and Marlie Packer, while Abby Dow has retired. The teams meet again on Friday in Ottawa.
Rugby.copy:
Forty-one matches, nearly four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but the Red Roses' unbeaten streak is over. It fell to the experienced Amy Cokayne to face the press this week after England lost their first match since 2022 against Canada.

"You can't dwell on it," said the Sale hooker, who has 95 international caps. "We weren't a million miles away, so it's not like we have to completely throw the book out - nothing needs to massively change to the way we play."

Rugby.title: Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup?
Rugby.summary: Wales boast a world-class scrum-half in Tomos Williams but Steve Tandy might have to assess his back-up before the 2027 World Cup.
bullets: Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams has started every Test he has been available for since Steve Tandy took charge in summer 2025, playing past the hour in every outing. He played 378 minutes in the 2026 Six Nations, compared with 357 for France's Antoine Dupont, 323 for Ireland's Jamison Gibson-Park and 302 for Scotland's Ben White.

Williams has shared matchday squads with only two other scrum-halves, Kieran Hardy and Reuben Morgan-Williams, and Hardy faces a lengthy lay-off with a knee injury. Dragons' Che Hope, 23, is among the options, though Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod urged caution. Gareth Davies, who retired from Test rugby in 2024 with 77 caps, has also been suggested as an emergency option. Wales open the 2027 World Cup against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October.
Rugby.copy:
There are few, if any, players more secure of a starting spot at next year's World Cup in Australia than Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams. France superstar Antoine Dupont has a rival for the nine jersey in Maxime Lucu, a talisman for back-to-back European champions Bordeaux-Begles.

Malcolm Marx, World Rugby player of the year, fights hard for his start as South Africa's hooker but must also be prepared for 'bomb squad' duty from the bench. The best players on the planet usually have a rival pushing them hard, but there is a gulf between 2025 British and Irish Lions tourist Williams and his fellow Welsh nines.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly: Prem clubs struggle in Europe
Rugby.summary: Danny, Ashy and Chris look back on round one of the Champions Cup.
Rugby.copy: Danny, Ashy and Chris reflect on a sombre opening weekend of the Champions Cup following the death of Lions and former Sale lock Hyron Andrews. They assess a chastening start for the Prem, with only one win from eight matches. Is it evidence of English rugby falling behind, or just a difficult opening weekend? Glasgow impress in the north west, Connacht turn on the style and Bath lose again. The Red Roses 41-match unbeaten run is over, but will the defeat to Canada prove to be a blessing in disguise? The All Blacks extend their winning run to 13 over the Wallabies and Spain enter the race to host the 2035 World Cup. Rugby in the Nou Camp anyone?

Rugby.title: Newcastle Red Bulls: Sale game is 'battle of North' even though Sharks 'really' midlands
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland says his side has their sights set on breaking their duck for the season and becoming Kings of the North by beating Sale Sharks on Friday night.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland says his side are aiming to secure their first win of the Gallagher PREM season against Sale Sharks on Friday night. Newcastle and Harlequins are the only winless teams, and four bonus points from the opening three games keep Newcastle off the foot of the table, five points behind seventh-placed Sale.

McFarland described the fixture as a "battle for the North", even though he said Sale are really in Cheshire, "sort of the Midlands". He acknowledged Sale have held primacy in recent years and have recruited well. Newcastle won 45-42 in May after recovering from 35-10 down, only their second win since 2 January. McFarland said the team is starting at the back of the grid but wants to pick off those ahead.
Rugby.copy:
Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland says his side has their sights set on breaking their duck for the season and becoming Kings of the North by beating Sale Sharks on Friday night.

The Red Bulls and Harlequins are the only two teams in the Gallagher PREM without a win this season, and the four bonus points they took in the opening three games are keeping them off the foot of the table.

Rugby.title: Nomadic Tommaso Allan has his sights set on playing in Australia next year
Rugby.summary: At 33, the utility back is intent on enjoying whatever the future holds.
bullets: Italy utility back Tommaso Allan, 33, has returned to his homeland by signing for Zebre Parma in the BKT URC, hoping the move will help him reach a fourth World Cup in Australia in just under a year. He has 91 caps and 552 points for Italy, making him the country's highest points scorer in both the Six Nations and the World Cup.

Born in Vicenza, Allan moved to England aged eight and played for Henley RFC and the Wasps Academy before joining Western Province in South Africa. He later played for Perpignan, Benetton and Harlequins, then returned to Perpignan before joining Zebre this summer. He has played at 10 and 15 for Zebre, whose next game is at Connacht on Friday. Allan said he is unsure how many years he has left but is enjoying a leadership role.
Rugby.copy:
After more than a decade of rugby wandering, Tommaso Allan is back in his homeland and determined to make the most of however long he has left in his career. Over the years, he has had spells playing in South Africa, France and England, as well as in his native Italy, while his 91 caps for the Azzurri have taken him around the world.

Now he has returned to the country of his birth by signing for Zebre Parma which means yet more border-hopping through being part of the multi-nation BKT URC. He is hoping the move will help him achieve his dream of playing in a fourth World Cup with a trip to Australia on the horizon in just under a year’s time.

Rugby.title: Leinster issue worrying injury update on Ireland No.8 Jack Conan
Rugby.summary: Leinster have confirmed that Ireland international Jack Conan has suffered a shoulder injury, casting fresh doubt over the province's back-row resources after Caelan Doris was already ruled out with a long-term foot and knee issue.
bullets: Leinster have confirmed that Ireland and British & Irish Lions No.8 Jack Conan suffered a shoulder injury in their 48-23 Investec Champions Cup Round 1 win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin. He was hurt while scoring a second-half try, and the province said he needs further assessment without giving a timeframe.

Caelan Doris is already out with a long-term foot and knee issue, leaving Leinster short in the back row. Jordan Larmour needs further assessment on a calf problem, and Hugh Cooney suffered a hand injury in the A game against Edinburgh. Leinster came back from 16-15 down at half-time by scoring 33 second-half points to secure a bonus-point win, and face Munster in the URC at the Aviva Stadium this weekend.
Rugby.copy:
Leinster have confirmed that Ireland international Jack Conan has suffered a shoulder injury, casting fresh doubt over the province’s back-row resources after Caelan Doris was already ruled out with a long-term foot and knee issue.

Conan was injured while scoring a crucial second-half try during Leinster’s impressive 48-23 Investec Champions Cup Round 1 victory over Clermont ASM at Stade Marcel-Michelin.

Rugby.title: SOS recruit: Exeter 'can't say that everything's signed, sealed, and delivered'
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has confirmed interest in signing Pumas lock André Goedhals to strengthen his injury-hit second row, but says the deal is far from done.
bullets: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has confirmed interest in signing Pumas lock André Goedhals, 21, to cover for Italian lock Andrea Zambonin, who faces a lengthy absence after a shoulder operation. Goedhals was born in Devon and holds a British passport, making him English-qualified. Baxter said the deal is not yet "signed, sealed, and delivered".

Goedhals grew up in Riversdale in the Western Cape, won Springbok under-20 honours and moved to the Pumas from the Stormers set-up. He was part of the Pumas side that lost the Currie Cup final 23-16 to the Griquas in Kimberley last month. Baxter said Exeter are waiting on the Pumas to complete the proper process in South Africa and that pushing it through quicker would be disrespectful.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has confirmed interest in signing Pumas lock André Goedhals to strengthen his injury-hit second row, but says the deal is far from done. Baxter says he has been looking to bring someone into his Sandy Park outfit since learning in the summer that Italian star Andrea Zambonin faced a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a shoulder operation.

He has also spoken with the Currie Cup franchise about a move for Goedhals, who holds a British passport after being born in Devon while his parents lived and worked in England, making him English-qualified.

Rugby.title: Nations Championship: November rugby returns to RugbyPass TV
Rugby.summary: On Friday 6 November, the inaugural Nations Championship returns with three consecutive rounds of fixtures that will determine who faces off for continental supremacy.
bullets: The inaugural Nations Championship resumes on Friday 6 November with three further rounds. France top the Northern Hemisphere table on twelve points, while South Africa lead New Zealand on points difference in the south. The Springboks scored the most points (130) and tries (20) in the opening rounds, and the two hemispheres are level with nine wins each.

Round 4 includes Ireland v Argentina at the Aviva Stadium, Scotland v New Zealand, and England v Australia at Twickenham. Round 5 features France v South Africa in Paris. The regular stage ends on 21 November with England v New Zealand, Ireland v South Africa and Fiji v Italy. Finals Weekend runs from 27 to 29 November, with all twelve nations playing and the title decider at 16:40 UTC on the final day.
Rugby.copy:
On Friday 6 November, the inaugural Nations Championship returns with three consecutive rounds of fixtures that will determine who faces off for continental supremacy. Heading into the home stretch, France sit top of the Northern Hemisphere table with twelve points, while back-to-back Rugby World Cup champions South Africa are ahead of the All Blacks on points difference on the Southern Hemisphere side.

With three more weeks of action to look forward to, RugbyPass looks back on the major takeaways from the opening rounds of the tournament and previews what’s to come. Unsurprisingly, Southern Hemisphere heavyweights New Zealand and South Africa put down early markers on home soil. The Springboks scored the most points (130) and the most tries (20) as they swept to three home victories. Their aerial dominance, set piece ability, and electric wingers proved too much for the opposition and will take some stopping if anyone hopes to rein in the world champions.

Rugby.title: Ex-Scotland captain Ritchie set for Glasgow debut
Rugby.summary: Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut this weekend.
bullets: Former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie is expected to make his Glasgow Warriors debut in Saturday's United Rugby Championship match against Benetton in Treviso. The 30-year-old flanker, capped 63 times, joined from French club Perpignan in the summer on a two-year deal. He has missed the start of the season with ankle and Achilles tendon problems and is now back in full training.

Assistant coach Nigel Carolan said the club had not wanted to rush Ritchie after summer surgery and a move to a new club. He said he would like Ritchie involved either starting or on the bench, ahead of Scotland's Nations Cup in a couple of weeks. Glasgow are second in the URC after three matches, behind Edinburgh, and face second-bottom Benetton.
Rugby.copy:
Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut. The former Edinburgh flanker signed from French club Perpignan in the summer but has been sidelined for the opening months of the season because of ankle and Achilles tendon issues.

The 30-year-old, capped 63 times, is now back in full training and is expected to play in Saturday's United Rugby Championship (URC) match against Benetton in Treviso. "He's training fully. We feel he's integrated into the systems now very well. And he's itching to go," said Carolan.

Rugby.title: Pat Lam explains sending Bristol Bears B team to Cape Town after Stormers hammering
Rugby.summary: Pat Lam, the Bristol Bears Director of Rugby, was candid in his assessment of the team's opening stanza of the season.
bullets: Bristol Bears Director of Rugby Pat Lam explained his decision to send the youngest and most inexperienced side he has selected to Cape Town for the Champions Cup opener, which Bristol lost 49-12 to the Stormers after leading 21-12 at one stage. Ellis Genge (injured), Louis Rees-Zammit, Fitz Harding and AJ MacGinty did not travel, and hooker Gabriel Oghre missed out with a calf strain.

Lam said the Champions Cup opening round was brought forward from December into October, and that the short turnaround before the Exeter match meant workloads had to be managed. He described it as probably Bristol's toughest first six games up to November and said no player can play six games in a row. He added that the young players, several from the Academy and most due to feature in the November Premiership Cup, would benefit from the experience.
Rugby.copy:
Pat Lam, the Bristol Bears Director of Rugby, was candid in his assessment of the team’s opening stanza of the season. As the only Premiership team to travel to South Africa and play a red-hot Stormers outfit in Cape Town in the opening round of the Champions Cup, Lam opted to prioritise the domestic league over Europe.

The trip to the Republic is sandwiched between Premiership encounters with Sale Sharks (an impressive 34-24 away win), Northampton Saints (a 41-26 win at home), an way loss to Saracens (7-30), along with two vital home fixtures against Exeter and Leicester Tigers.

Rugby.title: All Blacks have Springboks within their sights in World Rankings
Rugby.summary: Resounding back-to-back Bledisloe Cup wins have put the All Blacks within touching distance of the Springboks again at the top of the World Rugby Men's Rankings.
bullets: Back-to-back Bledisloe Cup wins of 50-19 in Auckland and 43-21 in Sydney have narrowed the gap between the All Blacks and the Springboks in the World Rugby Men's Rankings to 0.82 points. South Africa are on 93.09 and New Zealand on 92.27. Nearly four points separated the sides when the Springboks won the series 3-1 in Baltimore in mid-September.

The Springboks lost to the Wallabies later that month, and they cannot improve their rankings score when the Nations Championship resumes on 7 November because they face an Italian team outside the world's top 10. New Zealand could close the gap further by beating Scotland, who have never beaten the All Blacks. Scotland have moved above Australia into sixth place, with the Wallabies dropping to seventh after losing 0.46 points.
Rugby.copy:
Resounding back-to-back Bledisloe Cup wins have put the All Blacks within touching distance of the Springboks again at the top of the World Rugby Men’s Rankings. The 50-19 and 43-21 victories in Auckland and Sydney have closed the gap between rugby’s so-called greatest rivals to just 0.82 points, with the Springboks sitting on 93.09 points to New Zealand’s 92.27.

Nearly four points separated the teams when the Springboks wrapped up a 3-1 series win over the All Blacks in Baltimore in mid-September, but their defeat to the Wallabies later in the month, and New Zealand’s dominant Bledisloe Cup campaign has changed the picture.

Rugby.title: Wales great Evans to leave role as Lions chairman
Rugby.summary: British and Irish Lions are looking for a new chair as former Wales captain Ieuan Evans' term comes to an end after almost four years.
bullets: Ieuan Evans will stand down as chair of the British and Irish Lions on Wednesday after almost four years in the role. The former Wales captain was appointed in 2022 and is coming to the end of his term. He was tour manager last year when the men's team beat Australia in a series under Andy Farrell.

The Lions have begun searching for a new chair ahead of next year's inaugural women's tour to New Zealand. Evans, 62, said he was proud of the 2025 tour's success and of progress towards the first women's tour. He oversaw governance changes that brought independent directors onto the board. Chief executive Ben Calveley praised his passion for the Lions and understanding of the organisation.
Rugby.copy:
Ieuan Evans will stand down as chair of the British and Irish Lions on Wednesday after almost four years in the role. The former Wales captain, who played on tours to Australia in 1989, New Zealand in 1993 and South Africa in 1997, was appointed in 2022 and is coming to the end of his term.

Ex-wing Evans was tour manager last year when the men's team recorded a series victory against the Wallabies under Andy Farrell. The Lions have started the search for a new chair before next year's inaugural women's tour to New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Northampton 'security incident' believed to be a hoax
Rugby.summary: Police are investigating the incident at Saints' Franklin's Gardens "following threats made on social media".
bullets: A security incident during Northampton's 28-12 Champions Cup win over Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens on Sunday is believed to have been a hoax. Police were called to the stadium at about 19:00 BST following threats made on social media. The match had kicked off at 17:30, and players from both sides left the field straight after the final whistle as a precaution.

Northamptonshire Police said enquiries remain ongoing and that they are working closely with the club and policing partners. Northampton said they were sorry supporters did not get to see the players after the final whistle. The club added that the safety of supporters, players, staff and officials will always be its top priority.
Rugby.copy:
A 'security incident' during Northampton's Champions Cup win over Cardiff on Sunday is believed to have been a hoax. Police were called to the Saints' Franklin's Gardens stadium at about 19:00 BST "following threats made on social media".

The game had kicked off at 17:30 and players from both sides left the field straight after the final whistle as a "precautionary measure". "Enquiries into the incident remain ongoing and we are working closely with both the Saints and our policing partners on the investigation," said a Northamptonshire Police spokeswoman.

Rugby.title: Lions looking for new Chair with Ieuan Evans' time nearly up
Rugby.summary: The Welsh legend and World Rugby Hall of Famer was appointed in 2022 and says it has been "an enormous privilege" to serve the organisation, as a player and administrator.
bullets: Ieuan Evans' four-year tenure as Chair of the British and Irish Lions ends on Wednesday. Appointed in 2022, the Welsh former wing toured as a player in 1989, 1993 and 1997 and was tour manager in Australia last year. He called it "an enormous privilege" and cited the success of the 2025 Tour and progress towards the first Lions Women's Tour.

Lions CEO Ben Calveley praised Evans' passion for the organisation and the leadership he has shown as Chair. The Lions will appoint an Independent Chair in due course, with a further announcement to follow once the recruitment process concludes.
Rugby.copy:
Ieuan Evans’ tenure as Chair of the British and Irish Lions comes to a close on Wednesday after four years in the role. The Welsh legend and World Rugby Hall of Famer was appointed in 2022 and says it has been “an enormous privilege” to serve the organisation, as a player and administrator.

Evans went on three tours as a player – in 1989, 1993 and 1997 – and was the tour manager in Australia last year. “It has been an enormous privilege to serve as Chair of The British & Irish Lions. The Lions has played a hugely important part in my life, from the honour of representing the jersey as a player to helping shape its future as Chair,” he said.

Rugby.title: Former Wallabies coach Laurie Fisher takes on new Test role
Rugby.summary: The 68-year-old left his role with the Wallabies when Joe Schmidt handed over the head coach baton to Les Kiss in July.
bullets: Former Wallabies forwards coach Laurie Fisher, 68, is working as a consultant with the Zimbabwe national team ahead of their Test against Namibia in Harare this weekend. He left the Wallabies when Joe Schmidt handed the head coach role to Les Kiss in July. Former Exeter Chiefs skills coach Ricky Pellow has also joined head coach Pieter Benade's staff.

Zimbabwe, who appear at a Rugby World Cup for the first time since 1991 less than a year from now, identified the breakdown as an area for improvement after losing all three July Nations Cup matches. They play Samoa in Wakefield on 7 November, Uruguay at Ealing's Trailfinders ground on 14 November and Chile in Angoulême on 21 November. High Performance Director Liam Middleton said World Rugby helped secure Fisher's short-term services.
Rugby.copy:
Former Wallabies forwards coach Laurie Fisher is currently lending his expertise to the Zimbabwe national team as the Sables prepare for this weekend’s Test against Namibia in Harare.

The 68-year-old left his role with the Wallabies when Joe Schmidt handed over the head coach baton to Les Kiss in July, but is now back in the Test arena as a consultant to the African champions.

Rugby.title: Phil Dowson: 'Everyone at this time of year wants to go deep in both'
Rugby.summary: Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson praised his young players for stepping up after his much-changed team defeated Cardiff 28-12 in the Investec Champions Cup.
bullets: Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson praised his young players after a much-changed side beat Cardiff 28-12 in the Investec Champions Cup. Henry Pollock, Tommy Freeman and Alex Coles were rested and Fin Smith was on the bench. It was the first win in the competition by a Gallagher Prem team after seven failed attempts by fellow English sides.

Tries from James Pater and Toby Thame gave Northampton a 14-0 half-time lead. Harri Millard and Mason Grady scored for Cardiff to close within two points, before George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall tries secured victory. Dowson said everyone wants to go deep in both league and cup, so the squad's depth will be used. Northampton visit Leicester in the East Midlands derby next Saturday, while Cardiff face the Sharks next.
Rugby.copy:
Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson praised his young players for stepping up after his much-changed team defeated Cardiff 28-12 in the Investec Champions Cup. Dowson rested Henry Pollock, Tommy Freeman and Alex Coles and named Fin Smith on the bench for their European opener, with one eye on next Saturday’s East Midlands derby at Leicester.

Despite the changes, Northampton were able to finally record a first victory for a Gallagher Prem team in the competition after seven failed attempts from their fellow English sides.

Rugby.title: Five things we learned from the opening round of the Champions Cup as English sides struggle
Rugby.summary: Only one of the eight Prem entrants was successful on the first weekend of the competition
bullets: English clubs struggled in the opening round of the Investec Champions Cup, with only Northampton winning, 28-12 against Cardiff, while Gloucester secured a draw against defending champions Bordeaux-Bègles. Saracens were well beaten at Connacht, Bath lost to Montpellier, and Sale and Leicester were beaten by Glasgow and Pau respectively. Exeter performed well in Toulouse despite Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card.

Glasgow and Connacht impressed, with Sione Tuipulotu making 19 passes for the Warriors and Connacht benefiting from recruits Ciaran Frawley and Sam Gilbert. The Bulls and Stormers beat Stade Français and Bristol, though both opponents fielded weakened sides. The weekend was overshadowed by the sudden death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews on Friday, and by the tenth anniversary of Anthony Foley's death, which Munster marked with a win over Racing 92.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. The Investec Champions Cup campaign is underway with an intriguing opening round of action whetting the appetite for the season ahead.

This one-off weekend of fixtures serves only as an hors d’ouevres with the competition not resuming until after the Nations Championship in November, and the eight English clubs will have plenty to do when it picks up again.

Rugby.title: All Blacks winger ruled out for rest of 2026 as injury woes mount
Rugby.summary: Carter picked up the high-ankle injury in the act of scoring in the second half of the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park against the Wallabies.
bullets: Chiefs and All Blacks winger Leroy Carter will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign after ankle surgery. He suffered a high-ankle injury while scoring in the first Bledisloe Cup Test against the Wallabies at Eden Park, when Rob Valetini fell on his lower leg. He joins Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson and Ruben Love on the list of injured All Blacks ruled out for the rest of the year.

Ethan Blackadder, Patrick Tuipulotu, Richie Mo'unga, Shannon Frizell and Samisoni Taukei'aho are doubts for the end-of-year tour. Mo'unga is expected to be available for the final two Tests but is uncertain for the first two, against Scotland and Wales. The All Blacks are due to name a squad of 34 to 36 players on Tuesday NZT for a four-Test tour that also includes England in London and a finals weekend match at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.copy:
Chiefs and All Blacks winger Leroy Carter will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign after having ankle surgery following a nasty ankle injury at Eden Park. Carter picked up the high-ankle injury in the act of scoring in the second half of the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park against the Wallabies.

The winger charged towards the line after a Peter Lakai pop pass from the base of a ruck, before Wallabies loose-forward Rob Valetini fell on Carter’s lower leg in an attempt to stop the All Black from scoring.

Rugby.title: Perspective is needed on Wallabies thrashings, but RA must learn its lessons
Rugby.summary: Let’s not tiptoe around the lessons; they are black on white, and we have now seen them out in the open.
bullets: Back-to-back heavy defeats by the All Blacks have halted the momentum of the sixth-ranked Wallabies, who had gone six games unbeaten beforehand. The article argues the margins were probable because of factors known in advance and late injury and suspension issues, with the Wallabies unable to contend with a full-strength top-three side outside the World Rugby Regulation-9 window.

The piece calls on Rugby Australia to build better relationships with overseas clubs so coach Les Kiss can pick France-based Will Skelton, Taniela Tupou and Langi Gleeson, England-based Tom Hooper, and Japan-based Mark Nawaqanitawase, Jordan Petaia, Hunter Paisami and Samu Kerevi for the ANZAC weekend Bledisloe in 2027. It also says an experienced no.10 should be selected for November, noting the Wallabies kicked only 14 times in Sydney despite 56%-44% territory.
Rugby.copy:
The momentum behind the Wallabies has taken a couple of big hits with the back-to-back wallopings by the All Blacks. A previously six-game unbeaten streak had the Wallaby faithful and even some pundits wrongly proclaiming that ‘this was the best opportunity to win back the Bledisloe in years’.

The losses and the margins of those defeats were not only possible, but probable, because of factors known well in advance and late injury/suspension issues. Let’s not tiptoe around the lessons; they are black on white, and we have now seen them out in the open.

Rugby.title: The players who staked late claims for Wales spots
Rugby.summary: Dragons, Ospreys, Scarlets and Cardiff players give Wales boss Steve Tandy plenty to mull over before he names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday.
bullets: Wales head coach Steve Tandy names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday, 20 October, after Welsh clubs' European matches offered late evidence. Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets won their Challenge Cup openers, while Cardiff lost at Northampton on their return to the Champions Cup. Taulupe Faletau played almost an hour on his first outing since March, and Josh Adams came off the bench after injury.

Wales face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff, with another fixture against a southern hemisphere side at Twickenham on finals weekend. Tomos Williams is set to start at scrum-half against Japan on 7 November, with the replacement role open. Ospreys' Reuben Morgan-Williams made his first start of the season in Tbilisi, while Dragons' Aneurin Owen, uncapped at 25, was man of the match against Perpignan. Fly-half Sam Costelow came off with a hamstring injury, described as a precaution.
Rugby.copy:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday, 20 October and was given some late food for thought by the Welsh clubs in European action. Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets made winning starts in the Challenge Cup while Cardiff competed hard but lost at Northampton on their return to the top-tier Champions Cup.

Wales will face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff before another fixture at Twickenham against a southern hemisphere opponent on finals weekend. BBC Sport Wales looks at the players who grasped their last chance to make an impression on Tandy and his staff, as opportunities run out before the 2027 World Cup.

Rugby.title: Former Wallaroos captain calls time on eight-year international career
Rugby.summary: "Wallaroo #158 and the 19th Wallaroos captain, Emily’s work ethic and passion for the jersey means she has left it in a better place."
bullets: Former Wallaroos captain Emily Chancellor has announced her retirement from international rugby after eight years. The loose-forward, 35, will make her 41st and final appearance in the WXV Global Series Test against Scotland in Canberra this weekend. She debuted against the Black Ferns in Sydney in 2018, played at the 2021 and 2025 World Cups, and became the 19th Wallaroos captain in 2025.

Chancellor will remain available for the NSW Waratahs in the Swytx Super Rugby Women's competition. She said the time was right to leave the jersey open for the next generation and that she would cheer on the Wallaroos towards the 2029 home World Cup. Rugby Australia's Director of Women's High Performance, Tim Walsh, praised her work ethic and said she had left the jersey in a better place.
Rugby.copy:
The Wallaroos will be without their former captain after the Scotland Test in Canberra this weekend, with loose-forward Emily Chancellor calling time on her international career.

Wallaroos No.158 made her debut for Australia in 2018, three years after first being introduced to the national team environment. Chancellor captained the Wallaroos for the first time in 2025, becoming the 19th ever captain of the national side.

Rugby.title: Hurricanes secure 'ever improving' All Black prop until 2029
Rugby.summary: "I’m grateful to be with this club and to be part of the Hurricanes family,” Lauaki said.
bullets: The Hurricanes and New Zealand Rugby have signed new All Blacks prop Siale Lauaki until the end of the 2029 Super Rugby Pacific season, keeping him in New Zealand for the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour. The 23-year-old featured in three midweek matches on the All Blacks' tour of South Africa, making his tour debut against the Stormers in Cape Town.

Lauaki made his Hurricanes debut in 2024 against the Fijian Drua and has won two national titles with Wellington. Head coach Clark Laidlaw said the prop can play both sides of the scrum and adds consistency to a front row that includes Pasilio Tosi, Tyrel Lomax and Xavier Numia. Lauaki said he was grateful to a club that has given him many opportunities.
Rugby.copy:
The Hurricanes and New Zealand Rugby have secured the long-term services of new All Black prop Siale Lauaki. Lauaki has signed a deal until the end of the 2029 Super Rugby Pacific season, keeping him in New Zealand for the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour.

Lauaki was named in the All Blacks‘ 44-man squad to tour South Africa and featured on three occasions during the midweek matches. The prop made his All Blacks tour debut against the Stormers in Cape Town.

Rugby.title: Whitney Hansen: 'Six months ago we would have left 60 points out there'
Rugby.summary: Tuliau-Tua’a's four try-second half was proof of the system that Hansen is building, and how players out of the Farah Palmer Cup and Super Rugby Aupiki are being readied for the international game.
bullets: The Black Ferns beat France 81-12 in the first of three Tests at FMG Stadium Waikato in Hamilton, leading 43-0 at half-time. Maia Joseph scored the opening try and Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a scored four in the second half, while France replied only in the 60th minute through left-winger Léa Murie.

Head coach Whitney Hansen said her side was clinical, adding that six months ago they would have left 50 to 60 points unscored. She warned that the team was too passive in some collisions and expects a strong French response in Whangarei next weekend. Hansen has now won seven of her eight Tests in charge, and she highlighted the growth of young leaders such as Amarante Sititi, Braxton Sorensen-McGee and Tuliau-Tua'a in Ruahei Demant's recent absence.
Rugby.copy:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has given credit to her team for their clinical performance against France, where they piled on the points at FMG Stadium Waikato in Hamilton.

Hansen’s side claimed an 81-12 victory in the first Test of three against France, dominating from the first whistle. Black Ferns halfback Maia Joseph was the first to cross on a sunny afternoon in Hamilton, before backing it up six minutes later.

Rugby.title: Northampton beat Cardiff for first English win in Champions Cup
Rugby.summary: Northampton edge to a nervy Champions Cup pool win against tenacious Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens.
bullets: Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup, beating Cardiff 28-12 in Pool Four at Franklin's Gardens. They led 14-0 at half-time through tries from James Pater and Toby Thame. Harri Millard and Mason Grady narrowed the gap to two points, before George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall scored, though without securing a bonus point.

It was a difficult opening weekend for Prem clubs, with Gloucester drawing against champions Bordeaux-Begles and six other English sides losing. Cardiff, back in the top tier after two seasons in the Challenge Cup, rested several players but gave Taulupe Faletau and Josh Adams their first appearances of the season. Northampton visit Stade Francais in December, then Montpellier in January, before hosting Bulls. Cardiff host Bath in December.
Rugby.copy:
Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup by battling past Cardiff. Saints, quarter-finalists last season, scored four tries at Franklin's Gardens in a nervy Pool Four encounter.

The English champions led 14-0 at half-time thanks to efforts in tricky conditions by James Pater and Toby Thame. Tenacious Cardiff struck back through Harri Millard and Mason Grady to make it a two-point game in the final quarter.

Rugby.title: India Women records best-ever finish in Asian Rugby Sevens Series second leg
Rugby.summary: India Women records best-ever finish in Asian Rugby Sevens Series second leg Sportstar
bullets: The Indian women's rugby sevens team recorded its best performance at the Asian Rugby Sevens Series by finishing fifth in the second leg of the 2026 edition in Colombo, Sri Lanka, on Sunday 18 October. Captain Shikha Yadav and her side confirmed fifth place with a 19-12 victory over Thailand in the fifth-place classification match.

India finished second in its group behind Japan, ahead of UAE and Iran, then lost its quarter-final to Hong Kong-China before beating UAE and Thailand in classification matches. Shikha scored four tries, with Kalyani Patil and Mama Naik adding two each. Coach Paul Delport said the result, which included India's first-ever win over Thailand, showed the team can compete with established Asian sides. The men finished 11th, with one win in six matches.
Rugby.copy:

Shikha Yadav and Co. confirmed its fifth place finish with a 19-12 victory over Thailand in the 5th-place classification match. It finished second in its group behind Japan, and ahead of UAE and Iran. It lost its quarterfinal Hong Kong-China, but recovered to defeat UAE and Thailand in its classification matches.

Rugby.title: Toulouse survive red card to outlast Exeter in epic as English woes continue in Champions Cup
Rugby.summary: Toulouse overcame Rodrigue Neti’s sending off, while Leicester were well beaten by Pau as only Northampton won of the Prem clubs on the opening weekend
bullets: Exeter Chiefs lost 43-40 to 14-man Toulouse in the Champions Cup despite a hat-trick from Zack Wimbush. Toulouse prop Rodrigue Neti was shown a red card for a high tackle, and Exeter led 26-24 at half-time, but Toulouse went ahead through Matias Remue's late try and Henry Slade sent a penalty wide in the final moments.

Elsewhere, Leicester lost 41-17 at Pau despite tries from Ollie Chessum on his return from injury and Archie van der Flier, with Pau securing a bonus point. Northampton became the first Gallagher Prem side to win in this season's competition, beating Cardiff 28-12 at Franklin's Gardens after seven failed attempts by English clubs, with George Hendy named man of the match.

Rugby.title: Toulouse deny Exeter famous win as Slade misses last-gasp kick for draw
Rugby.summary: Toulouse deny Exeter Chiefs a famous Champions Cup victory in France, fighting back to win a frenetic contest with 14 men following Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card.
bullets: Toulouse beat Exeter Chiefs in a Champions Cup pool game despite playing most of it with 14 men after prop Rodrigue Neti was sent off in the 16th minute for shoulder-to-head contact on Ross Vintcent. Exeter's Zack Wimbush scored a hat-trick, but Toulouse took the lead while Ben Hammersley was in the sin-bin. Henry Slade pulled a late penalty from about 40 metres wide, so Exeter took only a losing bonus point.

The first half finished 26-24 to Exeter, with eight tries and two yellow cards. Matias Remue scored twice for Toulouse, with further tries from Ange Capuozzo, Joshua Brennan, Teddy Thomas and Romain Ntamack. Wimbush started on the wing in place of the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso. Will Butt, Jack Yeandle and Stephen Varney also scored for Exeter.
Rugby.copy:
Toulouse denied Exeter Chiefs a famous Champions Cup victory in France, fighting back to win a frenetic pool game with 14 men following Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card. Exeter had the chance to force a draw but, with the clock in the red, Henry Slade missed a penalty from about 40 metres out.

Zack Wimbush, starting on the wing for Exeter in place of injured England international Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, scored a hat-trick of tries as the 2020 champions fell just short of winning a classic contest.

Rugby.title: He scored five tries but could only think of a sixth
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb speaks to the Scrum V team about his ambitions for both club and country.
bullets: Wales wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb, 25, told the Scrum V podcast that even after scoring five tries in a game he would dwell on the one he missed. He represented England at under-20 level, began his professional career at Bath, spent time with Southland in New Zealand and scored 12 tries in 24 appearances for Cardiff without winning a Wales call-up before joining Leicester Tigers.

He made his Wales debut against Scotland in February, a defeat in Cardiff that he called "bittersweet", though the cap now hangs on his wall. Hamer-Webb was in Wales' summer squad but did not play, so he is still waiting for a second cap. He praised head coach Steve Tandy, said his confidence has returned at Leicester, and named a Premiership medal and a place at the World Cup in Australia as his goals.
Rugby.copy:
Gabriel Hamer-Webb could almost have a cigar in his hand. Reclined on a sofa at Leicester Tigers' training ground, dressed in casual sportswear, the Wales wing looks entirely at ease.

But there is an intensity to him. His large, friendly oval eyes are engaging, even as his gaze remains unwavering. He maintains eye contact, considers his answers carefully and speaks with striking precision.

Rugby.title: Struggling Quins pick up welcome Challenge Cup win
Rugby.summary: Harlequins shrug off poor form in the Prem to score a half-century of points against French side Vannes.
bullets: Harlequins opened their 2026-27 Challenge Cup campaign with a bonus-point win over French club Vannes, scoring nine tries to Vannes' three. Marcus Smith contributed 22 points from two tries and six conversions. Captain Cadan Murley and Will Evans each scored twice, with further tries from Will Hobson, Sam Riley and Jimmy Staples.

Quins are bottom of the Prem after losing all three league matches, while Vannes are bottom of the Top 14 with four defeats from four. It was Quins' first match at this stage of the competition since 2018. They have won the Challenge Cup a record-equalling three times, most recently in 2011. They host Saracens in a Prem derby next Sunday.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins put aside their difficulties in the early weeks of the new Prem season to start their 2026-27 Challenge Cup campaign with a welcome bonus-point win over French club Vannes.

Quins are bottom of the Prem after losing all three of their matches, but they were far too strong for their visitors, clocking up nine tries. England back Marcus Smith contributed 22 points courtesy of two tries and six conversions, while there were two tries from captain Cadan Murley and Will Evans and further efforts from Will Hobson, Sam Riley and Jimmy Staples.

Rugby.title: Late tries give Pau bonus-point win over Leicester
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers begin their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau.
bullets: Leicester Tigers began their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 Pool One defeat by Pau. Portugal international Rodrigo Marta scored two of the home side's five tries, and a late burst earned Pau a bonus point. Leicester's Ollie Chessum scored on his first appearance of the season after a foot injury, following a Billy Searle 50-22.

Pau scored three tries in a 20-minute spell either side of half-time, and Archie van der Flier's try cut the gap to seven points. Pau then scored 17 unanswered points, including a penalty from Axel Desperes and an interception try from Fabien Brau-Boirie. Marta is the Top 14's leading try-scorer this season with six in five appearances. Leicester's remaining pool matches are against Clermont Auvergne, Glasgow Warriors and Leinster.
Rugby.copy:
Leicester Tigers began their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau. Portugal international Rodrigo Marta crossed for two of the home side's five tries, with a late burst helping them earn a bonus point from their Pool One opener.

Despite falling behind to an early Pau penalty, Leicester did well in the early exchanges, their tactical kicking game keeping them camped in their opponents' territory. Billy Searle's 50-22 put the Tigers in superb field position and they capitalised through captain Ollie Chessum, who was making his first appearance of the season after recovering from a foot injury.

bullets: Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik conceded a walkover to Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun in the French Open men's doubles quarter-finals at the Arena Grand Paris, trailing 0-5 after two minutes. Coach Herry Iman Pierngadi said Wooi Yik injured his right leg in the first round against He Jiting and Ren Xiangyu, and the pair withdrew to avoid aggravating it. It was only their second tournament since reuniting, following a runner-up finish at the Denmark Open.

The withdrawal puts the world No. 4 pair's BWF World Tour Finals qualification at risk. They are seventh, holding one of eight places for the event in Hangzhou on 9-13 December, but are skipping the Hylo Open in Germany. Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin Rumsani beat world No. 1 Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae 21-15, 21-18 to reach the semi-finals, and have already qualified for the Finals.
Racket.copy:
PETALING JAYA: It should have been all celebrations for Malaysia at the French Open on Friday with both Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun and Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani checking into the penultimate stage of the French Open men’s doubles event.

World No. 5 Sze Fei-Izzuddin stunned world No. 1 Kim Won-ho-Seo Seung-jae of South Korea 21-15, 21-18 to book their place in the semi-finals. However, there was an undertone of worry in the other quarter-final match of the evening as former world champions Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik conceded a walkover to world No. 11 Wei Chong-Kai Wun after just two minutes on court.

Racket.summary: Britain's Hannah Klugman will face Elsa Jacquemot of France in Sunday's Lexus Wrexham Open singles final.
Racket.copy:
British teenager Hannah Klugman will face France's Elsa Jacquemot in Sunday's Lexus Wrexham Open singles final. Klugman, 17, won her semi-final 6-1, 6-4 against compatriot Jodie Burrage, to reach what will be the biggest match of her career.

She will face Jacquemot who overcame the Netherlands' Suzan Lamens 6-2, 7-6 to earn her spot in the final. Racket.title: French Open: Ubaidillah Bursts Lanier Bubble
Racket.summary: French Open: Ubaidillah Bursts Lanier Bubble BWF World Tour
Racket.copy:
Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah kept the French crowd waiting for a home celebration, beating Alex Lanier in a gripping semifinal to reach his first Super 750 final. Winning 21-16 16-21 21-17 against the world champion on home soil, Ubaidillah showed composure well beyond his 19 years. He was quick to the net, sharp and, above all, smooth and calm throughout.

“I’m very grateful to win. It was a very good match with Alex,” Ubaidillah told BWF. “I just tried to get into a good position and stay active.” “My key was to attack more and play at the front of the net,” he explained. “From that area, I could get into a more attacking position.”

Racket.title: Alcaraz faces Khachanov test in Vienna opener; Zverev meets Landaluce
Racket.summary: Alcaraz faces Khachanov test in Vienna opener; Zverev meets Landaluce ATP Tour
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz will likely have little time to find his indoor hard-court feet at the Erste Bank Open. The No. 3 player in the PIF ATP Rankings has been drawn against former Top-10 star and recent US Open semi-finalist Karen Khachanov at the ATP 500 event in Vienna. Alcaraz, who will compete in the Austrian capital for the first time since 2021, will be seeking a fast start to his European indoor swing after his third-round exit to Zizou Bergs at the Rolex Shanghai Masters.

Although Alcaraz will be wary of the threat posed by seven-time ATP Tour champion Khachanov, the Spaniard will enter the Vienna encounter with a 6-0 lead in the pair’s Lexus ATP Head2Head series. Should he extend his perfect record against Khachanov, Alcaraz would face Nikoloz Basilashvili or home wild card Jurij Rodionov in the second round, while seventh seed Tommy Paul is a potential quarter-final opponent.

bullets: PV Sindhu reached her second Super 750 final of the year by beating Japan's Hina Akechi 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 in the French Open semi-finals on Saturday 24 October. The match lasted one hour and 13 minutes. The 31-year-old Indian, ranked world number 11, won the Japan Open Super 750 title in July.

Sindhu will face Korea's world number one An Se Young in the final. She took the opening game in 18 minutes, claiming 11 of the final 12 points. Akechi, 21 and ranked 22nd, won the second game after saving no game points herself but converting her second chance at 22-20. Sindhu led throughout the decider and sealed victory with a cross-court smash on her fourth match point.
Racket.copy:
PV Sindhu battled past Japan's Hina Akechi in a gripping three-game semifinal to reach her second Super 750 final of the season. Double Olympic medallist shuttler PV Sindhu stormed into her second Super 750 final of the year with a thrilling win against Japan’s Hina Akechi at the French Open on Saturday, October 24.

The 31-year-old Indian, who clinched the Japan Open Super 750 title in July, showed tremendous composure to overcome world No. 22 Akechi 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 in a gruelling one-hour-and-13-minute encounter.

bullets: Katie Boulter lost 6-1 6-4 to doubles world number one Siniakova in the Japan Open semi-finals in Osaka, missing the chance to reach the final and a fifth WTA singles title. The eighth seed was swept aside in the first set and went a break up at the start of the second, but Siniakova claimed two breaks of her own to win in 85 minutes.

Boulter's run to the last four, which included a quarter-final win over Antonia Ruzic, will take her back above Sonny Kartal as British number one when the rankings are next updated. Kartal had moved ahead of her by reaching last week's Wuhan Open final. Siniakova will play 2023 champion Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final, after the American beat top seed Ann Li 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-3.

Racket.title: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign
Racket.summary: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign 조선일보
bullets: The Badminton World Federation announced that An Se-young has set a record by winning her 47th international singles title, passing Indonesia's Susi Susanti, who won 46. The BWF's count covers only titles since 1999, when it began compiling statistics, and excludes team events such as the Uber Cup. An has won nine individual titles this season from 11 tournaments entered.

An has held the world number one ranking for 106 consecutive weeks, 168 in total, with 122,287 points. She has reached the semi-finals of the BWF World Tour France Open (Super 750) in Paris, beating China's Han Yue 21-13, 21-16 in the quarter-finals. A fourth French Open title would be her 10th of the year and the first three-peat at the event since Pi Hongyan won in 2003–2005.
Racket.copy:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Kim Ga-eul] Japan has praised An Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), the "world's strongest," for her overwhelming skills. An Se-young is demonstrating formidable strength. She has won nine gold medals in individual events this season alone. Out of 11 international tournaments she participated in this season, she finished as runner-up at the All England Open, March, and withdrew in the round of 16 at the Japan Open, July, due to injury, but she claimed victory in all other events. An Se-young set a new record by reaching the top 11 times last year, tying the all-time single-season record for most wins in men's and women's singles with Kento Momota (Japan). At her current pace, she could set a new record.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) officially announced, "An Se-young has set a new record by winning her 47th international singles title." The previous record was held by Indonesia's badminton "legend" Susi Susanti, who had 46 wins. However, the BWF's count of singles titles only includes records since 1999 when it began compiling statistics. Additionally, team event results such as the Uber Cup (World Women's Team Badminton Championships) or the Asian Team Championships are excluded.

Racket.summary: Record 4 Malaysian doubles pairs in French Open semis Free Malaysia Today
bullets: A record four Malaysian doubles pairs have reached the semi-finals of the French Open, a BWF World Tour Super 750 event. Women's world number four pair Pearly Tan-M Thinaah beat Bulgaria's Gabriela and Stefani Stoeva 21-12, 21-15 and next face Japan's Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakashini. Men's world number five pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzudin Rumsani beat world number one pair Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae of South Korea 21-15, 21-18 in 36 minutes.

Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun reached the last four after a walkover, as compatriots Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik retired trailing 0-5 two minutes into the first game, with no official reason given. Malaysia has not won the men's doubles title since Gan Teik Chai-Koo Kien Keat in 2004. In the mixed doubles, Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing face China's world number six pair Guo Xin Wai-Chen Fang Hui in the semi-finals.
Racket.copy:
This is a record achievement at the prestigious BWF World Tour Super 750 championships. And history beckons for world No 4 Pearly Tan-M Thinaah, who could add a second title being the only Malaysian women’s doubles pair to have won the crown in the tournament’s 117-year history, in 2022.

Racket.title: Ashmita Chaliha Stuns Three-Time World Champion Akane Yamaguchi At French Open
Racket.summary: Ashmita Chaliha Stuns Three-Time World Champion Akane Yamaguchi At French Open News18
bullets: India's Ashmita Chaliha beat third seed and 2025 World Championships gold medallist Akane Yamaguchi 21-19, 21-18 in the second round of the French Open to reach the quarter-finals. It was the biggest win of her career. Chaliha, who won the Korea Masters earlier this year, had lost to Yamaguchi in the Denmark Open round of 16 last week, and had beaten China's Han Qian Xi 21-18, 24-22 in round one.

She will face either 11th seed Pornpawee Chochuwong or Nozomi Okuhara in the last eight. PV Sindhu also reached the quarter-finals, beating Riko Gunji in straight games, and will meet Chiu Pin-Chian or Sim Yu Jin. Elsewhere it has been a difficult week for Indian players: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, Unnati Hooda, Devika Sihag, Tanvi Sharma and Ayush Shetty all went out, and Lakshya Sen conceded a walkover.
Racket.copy:
Ashmita Chaliha produced the biggest victory of her career, stunning world champion and third seed Akane Yamaguchi in straight games to reach the French Open quarterfinals. Star Indian women’s singles shuttler Ashmita Chaliha, who won the Korea Masters earlier this year, stunned the 2025 World Championships gold medallist and third seed Akane Yamaguchi in the second round of the French Open to pull off the biggest win of her career.

Ashmita, who had beaten China’s Han Qian Xi in a 21-18, 24-22 first-round thriller on Tuesday, beat Yamaguchi in yet another close match, winning 21-19, 21-18. Ashmita was the underdog coming into this clash, having lost to the Japanese shuttler last week in the Round of 16 of the Denmark Open in what was their first-ever clash on tour.

Racket.title: Ahn Se-young extends 47-match win streak with French Open quarterfinal berth - CHOSUNBIZ
Racket.summary: Ahn Se-young extends 47-match win streak with French Open quarterfinal berth - CHOSUNBIZ Chosunbiz
bullets: World No 1 Ahn Se-young beat India's Tanvi Sharma 21-11, 21-14 in 37 minutes in the round of 16 of the BWF World Tour French Open (Super 750) at Arena Grand Paris, despite Achilles tendon pain. The win extended her winning streak to 47 matches and her season record to 63-1. She recovered from 1-5 down in the first game and 5-9 down in the second, having beaten Denmark's Amalie Schulz 21-6, 21-4 in the previous round.

Ahn, who is seeking a third consecutive French Open title, will face the winner of Han Yue and Mia Blichfeldt in the quarter-finals. A semi-final against Japan's Akane Yamaguchi is likely; Ahn beat her in the Denmark Open final and has now won 10 matches in a row against her. A French Open title would give Ahn her 10th title of the season, one short of the record of 11 she set last year.

Ahn Se-young defeated Sharma 2-0 (21-11, 21-14) in the round of 16 of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour French Open (Super 750) women's singles at Arena Grand Paris near Paris on the 22nd (KST) to advance to the quarterfinals. The match lasted 37 minutes.

Racket.title: By the numbers: Jovic beats Paolini for second time to reach Ningbo quarters
Racket.summary: By the numbers: Jovic beats Paolini for second time to reach Ningbo quarters WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
No. 4 seed Iva Jovic rallied from a break down in the opening set to defeat former world No. 4 Jasmine Paolini in straight sets and reach the quarterfinals of the BNB Ningbo Open on Thursday.

Paolini, a two-time Grand Slam finalist, broke early to take a 3-1 lead before Jovic found her rhythm. The American teenager broke twice to win the opening set 6-4. Jovic moved two breaks ahead at 4-1 in the second set, but Paolini fought back to cut the deficit to 4-3. Jovic held serve before breaking again to close out a 6-4, 6-3 victory in 1 hour, 22 minutes.

Racket.copy:
ATP Safe Sport prevented more than 234,000 abusive comments from reaching players and fans across ATP and player social media channels during the past year, helping protect the tennis community from online abuse.

Delivered in partnership with Tennis Data Innovations (TDI), sports technology company Sportradar, Social Protect and Arwen AI, ATP Safe Sport was launched in 2024 as part of the ATP's broader commitment to player welfare. Combining AI-enabled moderation, specialist threat assessment, investigations and collaboration with law enforcement authorities, the programme continues to evolve and strengthen its ability to protect players from online harm.

bullets: Emma Raducanu appears to have ended her 2026 season, with TV analyst Annabel Croft saying it would be "not a bad decision" because it lets her aim to be fully fit for 2027. The 2021 US Open winner last played in the Queen's Club Championship final on 14 June, losing in straight sets to Donna Vekic. She then withdrew from the Nottingham Open and Wimbledon with a grade four stress fracture in her right leg.

Raducanu missed the North American hard-court swing and is absent from the entry lists for the remaining Asian tournaments. She has fallen to No 109 after reaching the top 35 at Queen's, but could use a protected ranking to enter the main draw of up to eight events next year. Croft told Sky Sports Tennis that movement is central to Raducanu's game and must be fully recovered.

Racket.title: Marta Kostyuk’s Ningbo Open exit ends Race to Indian Wells as WTA Finals qualifiers confirmed
Racket.summary: The last qualifier for the WTA Finals has been confirmed. The post Marta Kostyuk’s Ningbo Open exit ends Race to Indian Wells as WTA Finals qualifiers confirmed appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Marta Kostyuk retired injured from her second-round match against Ekaterina Alexandrova at the WTA 500 Ningbo Open on Wednesday, trailing 6-4 in the first set after being broken in the opening game. The world No 10 has been dealing with a right wrist injury that forced her to miss the China Open, and she lost her opening match at last week's Wuhan Open to Maria Sakkari.

The exit ends Kostyuk's bid to qualify for the 2026 WTA Finals. She began the week 10th in the Race to Indian Wells, 815 points behind Karolina Muchova, who has now secured the final place and qualifies for the first time. Iga Swiatek, ninth in the Race, ended her season through injury. The Finals run from 8 to 15 November in Indian Wells, having been moved from Riyadh due to safety concerns.
Racket.copy:
Marta Kostyuk was forced to retire during her opening match at the Ningbo Open, and the result means the Race to qualify for the 2026 WTA Finals is now over. After receiving a first round bye at the WTA 500 tournament, No 3 seed Kostyuk began her campaign against 33rd-ranked Ekaterina Alexandrova in the second round on Wednesday.

Kostyuk retired due to injury after losing the first set 6-4 against her 31-year-old Russian opponent, having been broken in the opening game. The world No 10 has been dealing with a right wrist injury that forced her to miss the China Open, while she lost her opening match at last week’s Wuhan Open to Maria Sakkari.

Racket.title: Zizou Bergs responds to Carlos Alcaraz claiming he was ‘lucky’ after Shanghai upset
Racket.summary: Alcaraz said Bergs was "lucky" in certain moments after losing to the Belgian. The post Zizou Bergs responds to Carlos Alcaraz claiming he was ‘lucky’ after Shanghai upset appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Zizou Bergs has responded to Carlos Alcaraz's claim that he was "lucky" in their Shanghai Masters third-round match. The Belgian won 7-5, 7-6(4) over the world No 3, the biggest win of his career and his first against a top-three opponent. He then lost 7-6(5), 6-4 to Tommy Paul in the fourth round.

Speaking ahead of the ATP 250 event in Brussels, Bergs said a player's press-conference words should not be taken literally and that he was "not too worried" about the comments. He said the victory and earlier challenges to Alcaraz had given him confidence. Alcaraz had called his own level "really bad" while praising Bergs's. The 27-year-old, ranked 41, opens against world No 96 Toby Samuel in Brussels.
Racket.copy:
Zizou Bergs has responded to Carlos Alcaraz’s “lucky” comment after his upset victory over the Spaniard at the 2026 Shanghai Masters. The Belgian stunned world No 3 Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6(4) in the third round in Shanghai last week to earn the biggest win of his career to date.

It was Bergs’ third career win over a top 10 player, but his first against an opponent ranked in the top three. He had lost his only previous encounter against Alcaraz at the 2025 Japan Open.

Racket.title: Rafael Nadal told ‘your time will come’ as Toni Nadal reveals his coaching dream
Racket.summary: Is it only a matter of time before Rafael Nadal becomes Spain's Davis Cup captain? The post Rafael Nadal told ‘your time will come’ as Toni Nadal reveals his coaching dream appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Toni Nadal believes his nephew Rafael Nadal would make a good Spain Davis Cup captain and that his time will eventually come. Speaking on Ondacero's Radioestadio Noche, he said he thought Rafael would like the role at some point and described him as someone who brings a team together. Rafael won five Davis Cup titles with Spain (2004, 2008, 2009, 2011 and 2019) and had a 37-6 record.

Marc Lopez will succeed David Ferrer as captain from the start of 2027 on a three-year contract to December 2029. Ferrer, who took over from Sergi Bruguera in January 2023, steps down after this year's Davis Cup event in Bologna in November. Toni Nadal called the 44-year-old's promotion a reward for great players. Lopez, a former doubles world No 3, was part of Rafael Nadal's coaching team from 2021 to 2024.
Racket.copy:
Toni Nadal believes Rafael Nadal will make a good Davis Cup captain as he is someone “who brings a team together” as he suggested it is only a matter of time before the tennis great throws his hat into the ring for the Spain job.

Spain will have a new Davis Cup captain from 2027 onwards as Marc Lopez will take over David Ferrer – who succeeded Sergi Bruguera in January 2023 – at the start of 2027 after the latter announced last week that he would step down after this year’s event in Bologna, Italy, in November.

Racket.title: Boulter produces emphatic win at Japan Open
Racket.summary: Britain's Katie Boulter claims a dominant win in her rain-affected first-round match against Himeno Sakatsume in the Japan Open.
bullets: Katie Boulter beat Japan's Himeno Sakatsume 6-3 6-1 in the first round of the Japan Open in Osaka, completing the match on Tuesday after rain halted play on Monday with her a set and 3-1 up. The 30-year-old took five of nine break points and saved all but one of the 13 she faced. She will play Switzerland's Viktorija Golubic in the second round.

Boulter said the interruption made for a tough place to stop, and that she had to reset her mindset on Tuesday and focus on getting over the line without a third set. Separately, Iga Swiatek, the world number nine, has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open with a thigh injury, a setback to her hopes of reaching the WTA Finals in Indian Wells from 8-15 November.
Racket.copy:
Katie Boulter claimed a dominant win in her rain-affected first round match against Himeno Sakatsume in the Japan Open. The British player was a set and 3-1 up against the home favourite when play was halted because of bad weather in Osaka on Monday.

She completed the win on Tuesday as she secured a 6-3 6-1 victory. "Yesterday was a tough spot to end at," said Boulter, who will play Viktorija Golubic of Switzerland in the second round.

bullets: World No. 1 An Se-young will defend her French Open title at the Super 750 event in Paris (20–25 October), after the Korea Badminton Association confirmed she has no major injury. She had complained of right Achilles tendon pain and slipped in the Denmark Open final, which she won 21-18 in the third game against Akane Yamaguchi for her ninth title of the season and 47th career title.

She opens against Denmark's Amalie Schulz, world No. 44, who came into the draw after Japan's Tomoka Miyazaki withdrew with an injury sustained in Denmark. The reseeding allowed P. V. Racket.copy:

Racket.summary: Elina Svitolina and Iga Swiatek won't feature at the Ningbo Open. The post Ningbo Open withdrawal list: Elina Svitolina and Iga Swiatek among 6 stars to pull out of WTA 500 event appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The 2026 Ningbo Open has lost three of its five WTA top-10 players, with Elina Svitolina and Iga Swiatek the latest to withdraw. World No 6 Svitolina pulled out on Friday and was replaced by Anhelina Kalinina. Swiatek, the second seed, withdrew with a thigh injury, so lucky loser Anastasia Zakharova goes straight into the second round against Marie Bouzkova.

Jessica Pegula withdrew to focus on her health, which moved Leylah Fernandez into the main draw. Anna Kalinskaya withdrew through illness, and newly crowned Wuhan Open champion Maja Chwalinska pulled out citing physical fatigue. Elena Rybakina and Marta Kostyuk remain in the field at the Yinzhou Tennis Centre. Pegula and Kalinskaya have also withdrawn from the Pan Pacific Open in Japan.
Racket.copy:
The 2026 Ningbo Open was due to feature five WTA top-10 players, but that total is down to just two with Elina Svitolina and Iga Swiatek among the big-name stars to withdraw from the tournament.

The duo were due to join world No 1 Elena Rybakina, No 4 Jessica Pegula and No 10 Marta Kostyuk in the star-studded WTA 500 line-up at the Yinzhou Tennis Centre this week. World No 6 Svitolina withdrew from the tournament on Friday with the decision coming just 48 hours before she announced the shock news that her marriage with former ATP star Gael Monfils is ending.

She has also slipped to No. 4 in the British rankings, behind Sonay Kartal, who rose 121 places to No. 49 after reaching the Wuhan Open final, and ahead of Katie Boulter and Fran Jones in the new order.

Kartal beat Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini and Elina Svitolina on the way to the final, where she lost in three sets to Maja Chwalinska. Raducanu is undecided on whether she will play again this year and is likely to spend the next three months rehabbing, with a return in 2027. Racket.title: UK's largest indoor tennis event returns to Wrexham
Racket.summary: The Wrexham Open returns as some of tennis' biggest rising stars head to north Wales in search of glory.
bullets: The Wrexham Open, billed as the UK's largest indoor tennis event, returns this week as a W100 ITF World Tennis Tour tournament running from 18 to 25 October. It is set to be the UK's biggest women's tournament outside the grass-court season this year. Anna Blinkova, a former top 40 player, is top seed, and the field includes former top 50 players Mona Barthel, Anna-Lena Friedsam and Rebecca Sramkova.

Armenia's Alina Charaeva, who beat world number one Elena Rybakina and 2024 Wrexham winner Sonay Kartal at the China Open this month, is among the entrants. Wales' Mimi Xu won both the singles and doubles titles in 2025, the latter alongside Ella McDonald, but is not defending them and is instead playing the W75 Saguenay event in Canada. British players including Alicia Dudeney, Hannah Klugman and Daniella Britton are in the draw.
Racket.copy:
The UK's largest indoor tennis event returns this week some of the biggest rising stars head to the Wrexham Open in search of glory. Among them is Armenia's Alina Charaeva, who made headlines by beating world number one Elena Rybakina in the China Open earlier this month.

The 24-year-old also beat 2024 Wrexham Open winner Sonay Kartal at the China Open. The home crowd in Wrexham were treated to a Welsh winner in both the singles and doubles event in 2025, as Wales' Mimi Xu claimed both titles - alongside Ella McDonald.

Racket.title: Iga Swiatek pulls out of Ningbo Open: What it means for her WTA Finals chances
Racket.summary: Iga Swiatek's WTA Finals hopes suffer fatal blow. The post Iga Swiatek pulls out of Ningbo Open: What it means for her WTA Finals chances appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the WTA 500 Ningbo Open with a left thigh injury, which ends her hopes of qualifying outright for the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. She aggravated the problem in her Wuhan Open semi-final defeat to fellow Pole Maja Chwalinska, ignoring calls from her physiotherapist to retire, and was left 545 points behind Karolina Muchova, who holds the final qualifying place.

Even a win at the Pan Pacific Open would leave the 25-year-old 45 points short of Muchova. She is still expected to qualify as one of two alternates, alongside Marta Kostyuk, but may end her season early. It is the first time since 2019 that the 2023 WTA Finals champion has failed to qualify, and she is eighth in the rankings.
Racket.copy:
Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open due to an injury and the decision has had a major impact on her hopes of qualifying for the WTA Finals. The six-time Grand Slam winner struggled with a left thigh injury during her Wuhan Open semi-final match against fellow Pole Maja Chwalinska and she ignored calls from her physiotherapist to retire from the match.

She went on to lose in straight sets with result putting a major dent in her chances of competing at the season-ending tournament in Indian Wells. And that injury has proven to be more serious as she has been ruled out of the WTA 500 event in Ningbo, which ends her hopes of qualifying for the WTA Finals as one of the top-eight players.

Racket.title: Alex Eala defended after ‘harsh’ fan criticism due to poor WTA form recently
Racket.summary: Eala has suffered on the WTA Tour's Asian swing. The post Alex Eala defended after ‘harsh’ fan criticism due to poor WTA form recently appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alex Eala won her opening match at the Ningbo Open, beating Diane Parry in straight sets, after early exits in Singapore and Wuhan and a failure to win gold for the Philippines at the 2026 Asian Games. The slump followed her best spell of the year, when she won her first title at the Washington Open, reached the Berlin semi-finals and the fourth round at Wimbledon.

Filipino pole vaulter Ernest Obiana defended her on Instagram after criticism of her results, saying athletes have good and bad days and that harsh comments do not help them return stronger. In the second round Eala will face the winner of Yulia Putintseva against Diana Shnaider, with Iva Jovic a likely third-round opponent. Eala has lost all three previous meetings with Jovic. The tournament runs until 25 October.
Racket.copy:
Alex Eala returned to winning ways at the Ningbo Open, as she defeated Diane Parry in straight sets to confirm her place in the second round of the tournament. Prior to her victory in Ningbo, Eala was enduring an Asian swing to forget, however, as she suffered early exits in Singapore and Wuhan, as well as failing to win the gold medal for the Philippines at the 2026 Asian Games.

Eala’s first true rough patch on the WTA Tour came after her most fruitful spell in the summer, as she won her first title at the Washington Open and reached the semifinals of the Berlin Open and the fourth round of Wimbledon.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev hits another major ranking landmark ahead of becoming world No 1
Racket.summary: Another achievement for Zverev! The post Alexander Zverev hits another major ranking landmark ahead of becoming world No 1 appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev has reached his 300th week inside the ATP top five, a milestone only 15 players have managed since 1973. He is 23 weeks short of equalling Mats Wilander's total and sits well ahead of Carlos Alcaraz (222 weeks) and Jannik Sinner (160). He won Roland Garros and the US Open this year and is confirmed as year-end world No 1 because Sinner has ended his season early.

Zverev lost the Shanghai Masters semi-final to Alejandro Davidovich Fokina and admitted afterwards that he was tired, saying he had one day off after the US Open and felt flat from the Bublik match onwards. He went straight from the US Open to Davis Cup duty for Germany, then played Beijing and Shanghai. He is expected to play the Vienna Open from 30 October, though a withdrawal to prepare for the Paris Masters and ATP Finals would not be a surprise.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev is enjoying his best-ever moment in the ATP Tour rankings at present. The German has come of age this year by winning Roland Garros and the US Open and it’s helped him soar to the top of the rankings.

Zverev might not be the world No 1 yet, but he has already been confirmed to reach the summit of the ATP Tour and stay there as the year-end world No 1 due to Jannik Sinner ending his season early.

bullets: Gael Monfils brought forward his retirement after Elina Svitolina ended their marriage, according to a report in L'Equipe. The International Tennis Integrity Agency added the 40-year-old Frenchman to its retired list last week after he removed himself from anti-doping protocols on 5 October, meaning he can no longer enter tournaments. He had been removed from the Lyon ATP 250 entry list for "personal reasons".

Monfils had said in October last year that 2026 would be his final season, with the Paris Masters planned as his farewell. L'Equipe journalist Franck Ramella wrote that the news hit him "like a ton of bricks" and that he could no longer play. His second-round loss to Learner Tien at the US Open appears to have been his last match. A return would require six months of out-of-competition testing.
Racket.copy:
Gael Monfils decided to retire from tennis earlier than planned due to Elina Svitolina’s decision to end their marriage, according to a report. Last week, the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) added Monfils to its ‘retired’ list and confirmed the Frenchman had removed himself from the sport’s anti-doping protocols — meaning he is no longer eligible to enter tournaments.

The head of communication at the ITIA told French sports newspaper L’Equipe: “He (Monfils) informed us about it; he is now considered retired and is no longer authorised to participate in tournaments.
