Racket.title: Elena Rybakina outlines her main WTA Tour goal for the rest of the 2026 season
Racket.summary: Rybakina is set for Ningbo Open action. The post Elena Rybakina outlines her main WTA Tour goal for the rest of the 2026 season appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: World No 1 Elena Rybakina has said her main goal for the rest of the 2026 season is to finish the year as number one, while managing her health and fitness. She has not won a match since lifting the US Open title in September, losing her opening match at the China Open to Alina Charaeva. She faces the winner of Cristina Bucsa and Polina Kudermetova in the second round of the Ningbo Open.

Rybakina will then defend her WTA Finals title, which she won by beating Jessica Pegula and Aryna Sabalenka in the knockout rounds. No player has won back-to-back titles since Serena Williams in 2013 and 2014. This year's event is at Indian Wells, moving from Riyadh, from 8 to 15 November. Gauff, Sabalenka, Andreeva, Noskova, Svitolina and Pegula have also qualified.
Racket.copy:
Elena Rybakina has undoubtedly been the best player on the WTA Tour this year stastically, but she has produced some strange performances and endured some strange results. The star is yet to taste victory since lifting the US Open title in September, having lost her opening round match at the China Open to Alina Charaeva.

That was not the only early exit Rybakina has suffered in 2026 either, as she was beaten in the opening round of the Berlin Open and the second round of Roland Garros. Rybakina is looking to return to winning ways at the Ningbo Open, which is the penultimate WTA 500 tournament of the 2026 season.

Racket.title: Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
Racket.summary: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.
bullets: Ukrainian tennis player Elina Svitolina, 32 and ranked sixth in the world, has announced the end of her marriage to French former player Gaël Monfils, 40. In an Instagram post she cited the emotional impact of the war in Ukraine, saying she needs to find her way back to herself and could not do so within the marriage.

Svitolina said Monfils listened and respected her needs with strength and grace. The couple married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter, Skai, who Svitolina said will always come first, adding that the marriage is ending but the family is not. She grew up in Odesa, which has been heavily bombed by Russia since its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Racket.copy:
Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player Gaël Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country.

The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside". "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage.

Racket.summary: It's someone Carlos Alcaraz knows well. The post Carlos Alcaraz’s next Davis Cup coach confirmed after David Ferrer’s departure appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: David Ferrer has announced that the 2026 Davis Cup will be his last as Spain captain after four years in charge, citing solely personal reasons and a desire to start a new stage. Marc Lopez, already part of the Spain Davis Cup setup, will take over the team from 2027.

Spain have not won the Davis Cup under Ferrer, but are among the favourites at this year's Finals in Bologna from 24 to 29 November, where they will compete against South Korea, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Austria, Czech Republic and Canada. Alejandro Davidovich Fokina and Rafael Jodar, who both reached the Shanghai Masters final, are in contention for selection alongside Carlos Alcaraz, Marcel Granollers and Pedro Martinez. Czechia's Vojtěch Strejček and Lukáš Thor reached the quarter-finals.

The 6ft 7in player beat the likes of Felix Auger-Aliassime, Holger Rune, and Ben Shelton at the Swiss Indoors, as his booming serve proved too hot to handle. bullets: Sonay Kartal, 24, became British number one on Monday after reaching the Wuhan Open final in only her third tournament back from a stress fracture in her back. Using a protected ranking, she rose from 170th to 49th by earning 650 points, and became the first British player to reach a WTA 1000 final since Johanna Konta in 2019. She lost the final to French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Kartal said she was unable to walk without pain for about the first month of her injury and credited coach Ben Reeves, fitness coach Ian Aylward and physio Dani Gillanders. Regaining her ranking means she will no longer need a protected ranking for events including the 2027 Australian Open. She withdrew from the Japan Open in Osaka, saying the goals of her Asian swing had been achieved.
Racket.copy:
Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not stand up and brush her teeth without "being in agony". The pain caused by a stress fracture in her back eventually subsided, but the 24-year-old Briton still had a long road to full recovery, which needed to be navigated with patience and hard work.

Kartal did not make her return to competitive action until little under a month ago. But on Monday, she became the new British number one after an extraordinary week at the Wuhan Open, where she reached the biggest final of her career in just her third tournament back.

Racket.title: Denmark Says Thank You to Axelsen

bullets: Danish badminton paid tribute to Viktor Axelsen in his home city of Odense on Sunday at the SJF Bank Arena, where he was presented with flowers. Odense Mayor Peter Rahbaek Juel and Badminton Denmark Chief Executive Kristian Pihl delivered tributes, with Pihl thanking Axelsen for the journey, the memories and everything he had given Danish badminton.

Axelsen's achievements include two Olympic gold medals, two world titles, four European crowns and a place in the Danish team that won the country's first Thomas Cup in 2016. He also spent years at the top of the world rankings in men's singles. Thanking fans, sponsors, family and friends, he said he started playing in Odense and almost hit his last shuttlecock there as well.
Racket.copy:
Danish badminton paid tribute to its greatest modern player Viktor Axelsen in his home city of Odense on Sunday. At the SJF Bank Arena, Axelsen was presented with flowers before receiving heartfelt tributes from the Mayor of Odense Peter Rahbaek Juel and Badminton Denmark Chief Executive Kristian Pihl. Their message was simple.

“We have come together to say thank you,” said Pihl. “Thank you, Viktor for the journey, the memories and everything you have given Danish badminton.” For nearly two decades, Axelsen carried Danish hopes on the biggest stages in world sports. He became a global ambassador for badminton, inspired a new generation of players and built a legacy few can match.

Racket.copy:

Eleven of the next 12 points fell her way and suddenly there was no stopping the world No.1 from claiming her 47th title. The triumph, a hard-fought 21-23 21-14 21-18 victory over Akane Yamaguchi in the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 final, made her the most decorated women’s singles player in international badminton, moving one title clear of Indonesian great Susi Susanti.

Racket.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My parents were very hard to please, but it shaped my resilience” - How Emma
Racket.summary: Inspiring story of the day: “My parents were very hard to please, but it shaped my resilience” - How Emma The Times of India
bullets: Emma Raducanu won the 2021 US Open at the age of 18 without dropping a set in 10 matches, becoming the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title. She won three qualifying matches and seven main-draw rounds, beating Greece's Maria Sakkari in the semi-finals and Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 6-3 in the final.

Raducanu has said her strict upbringing in Bromley, south London, built her resilience. Her Romanian father Ian and Chinese mother Renee Zhai, both of whom worked in finance, set high expectations, and she earned an A* in mathematics and an A in economics at A-level in 2021. She said her parents' limits on her social life left her comfortable in her own company, and credits her mother's 'step by step' advice for her calmness.
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu made tennis history at 18 when she won the 2021 US Open without dropping a set in 10 matches, becoming the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title. Her success came after years of balancing tennis training with schoolwork and living under her parents’ high expectations. Born in Toronto to Romanian father Ian Raducanu and Chinese mother Renee Zhai, she moved to England as a young child. Raducanu has often spoken about how her strict upbringing helped her become more independent, focused and resilient.

How did Ian Raducanu and Renee Zhai shape Emma Raducanu’s childhood? Emma Raducanu grew up in Bromley, south London, in a family that placed a strong focus on education and hard work. Her father, Ian, is Romanian, while her mother, Renee, is Chinese. Both worked in finance and encouraged their daughter to take her responsibilities seriously, both in the classroom and on the tennis court.

bullets: Rafael Jodar lost the Shanghai Masters final 1-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 to fellow Spaniard Alejandro Davidovich Fokina on Sunday, having come within two points of victory in the second-set tiebreak. The 20-year-old world No 13 earned 650 ranking points as runner-up, lifting him from 11th to ninth in the Race to Turin on 3,159 points. He now leads De Minaur in 10th by 279 points and Novak Djokovic in 11th by 319.

The top eight in the Race qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin, but Jannik Sinner, second in the Race, will not play again in 2026, so ninth place is now the final qualifying spot. Jodar is 166 points behind Arthur Fils in eighth, 221 behind Frances Tiafoe in seventh and 261 behind Daniil Medvedev in sixth. Croft said a break would let Raducanu heal fully, rest and start next year fit, adding that health is the most important factor.

The 23-year-old is ranked 107th, having dropped out of the top 100, and has played 21 matches in 2026, winning 11. She lost in the second round of the Australian Open to Anastasia Potapova and in the first round of the French Open to Solana Sierra. She would have become the second Briton after Johanna Konta to win a WTA 1000 title, and had been ranked 170th before the event after a six-month lay-off with a back injury.

Kartal's run, which included wins over Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko, returns her to the top 50 and makes her British number one on Monday. Nevertheless, it has still been a remarkable week for Kartal, the best in her career so far, after only returning to the tour earlier this month following a six-month lay-off due to a back injury.

bullets: Jon Rahm received $26m from LIV Golf in the year before the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 8 September, court records filed in New Jersey show. Bryson DeChambeau was paid nearly $13.9m and Dustin Johnson $10.7m, while LIV also paid seven executives $15.6m in retention money. Chief executive Scott O'Neil received more than $13.6m between September 2025 and August 2026.

Contractors including Fresh Tape Media ($1.23m), Mobii Systems (over $1.1m) and Deltatre (nearly $860,000) say they are still owed money, and players are among the largest unsecured creditors, with Rahm owed about $7.5m. Rahm has reached a separation agreement releasing LIV from monetary claims, which a judge is due to consider on 5 November. LIV is seeking to relaunch as LIV 2.0 with up to $300m from BC Partners Credit, subject to O'Neil signing enough players by a deadline of 25 October that can be extended.
Golf.copy:
Spanish golfer Jon Rahm received $26 million from LIV Golf in the year before the Saudi-backed league filed for bankruptcy, as it also paid seven of its executives $15.6 million in retention money while contractors went unpaid, court records show.

The figures are in documents filed late Thursday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey, where LIV sought Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8. The payments to players also include nearly $13.9 million to American Bryson DeChambeau, the 2024 U.S. Open champion, and $10.7 million to Dustin Johnson, a former world No. 1. Australian Cameron Smith and American Bubba Watson each received about $2.5 million.

Golf.summary: Yuri Yoshida Wins in Republic of Korea for Her First LPGA Tour Victory LPGA
bullets: Yuri Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament at Pine Beach Golf Links in Haenam on Sunday, taking her first LPGA Tour title. The 26-year-old Japanese player finished on 17-under 271, one shot ahead of overnight leader Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi, who both ended on 16 under. Yoshida began the final round four shots off the lead and opened with an eagle at the par-5 second hole.

Ryu led by four strokes going into the final round but shot a 73, and both she and Yoshida bogeyed the 18th. Choi remains without a win in 125 LPGA Tour starts, having held or shared a 54-hole lead five times, and was runner-up in Shanghai the previous week. Defending champion Sei Young Kim tied for 55th. The tour moves to Kuala Lumpur next week for the Maybank Championship, the third of four events in its Asian swing.
Golf.copy:
HAENAM, South Korea (AP) — Yuri Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament holding off Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi in a close finish at Pine Beach Golf Links on Sunday. It was Yoshida’s first LPGA Tour victory and came in dramatic finale as both overnight leader Haeran Ryu and Yoshida bogeyed the final hole leaving the Japanese player ahead by one stoke and a four-round total of 17-under 271.

Yoshida was four shots off the pace going into Sunday’s final round but lit up the front nine with an eagle at the par-5 second, followed by three consecutive birdies to be 5-under 31 at the turn. Bogey’s at the 15th and 18th was offset by a crucial birdie at the 17th which gave the 26-year-old the buffer she needed.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf paid executives $15.6 million as vendors went unpaid, while Cam Young signed intent with LIV new bankruptcy filings show Golf Digest
bullets: LIV Golf paid $15.6m in retention payments to executives before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, according to court documents. CEO Scott O'Neil received a $6.375m retention bonus on 24 June and was paid more than $13.6m between 12 September 2025 and 28 August 2026. CFO David Phillips was paid more than $3.3m and chief legal officer John Ruzich about $2.6m, while founding commissioner Greg Norman received more than $9.4m when he left in September 2025.

The payments came as LIV failed to pay vendors, prompting lawsuits including Fresh Tape Media seeking $1.23m and Mobii Systems claiming more than $1.1m. The filings also show Cameron Young signed an intent to play for LIV after the 2022 Open. The deadline for players to commit to LIV 2.0 is Sunday 25 October. A LIV attorney told the court the league expects to know by the end of the month whether it will proceed, with up to $300m of financing from BC Partners.

Golf.title: LIV's latest court filings paint clearest picture of league's lavish spending
Golf.summary: LIV Golf's most recent bankruptcy court filings are a reminder of just how much money it takes to run a flashy golf league. The post LIV’s latest court filings paint clearest picture of league’s lavish spending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Bankruptcy filings are notoriously cumbersome, but every bankruptcy judge would admit the tedious paperwork is necessary. If a company is declaring bankruptcy, and thereby seeking some sort of legal protection against its current state, it had better be able to explain why.

But the process of doing so is a nightmare for lawyers as much as it is for their printers. It doesn’t take long for the number of pages to cross the threshold of tens of thousands. On Thursday evening alone, thousands of pages were filed in LIV Golf’s bankruptcy case, across its lot of international entities, its 13 franchises and dozens of other subsidiaries. Staring at it might send you into a daze, but there’s plenty that can be gleaned from these documents, which were prepared by LIV’s management and advisors. Thursday’s trove offered one main theme: LIV Golf owed many companies money.

Golf.copy:
Jarvis and Rozner lead, the battle for a Tour card comes to an emotional end for some, while others keep their hopes alive at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club. Here's what you need to know from the second round of the Genesis Championship in South Korea.

Antoine Rozner made two birdies in his final three holes to catch first-round leader Casey Jarvis as the pair head into the weekend of the Genesis Championship in a share of the lead.

Golf.title: DP World Tour stalwarts suffer card heartbreak
Golf.summary: DP World Tour stalwarts suffer card heartbreak Sky Sports
bullets: Casey Jarvis shares the halfway lead at the Genesis Championship at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club with Antoine Rozner, both on 10 under after rounds of 67 and 65 respectively. A win would lift Jarvis, a two-time DP World Tour winner this season, above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy to second in the Race to Dubai. Open champion Ryan Fox is three strokes back and sixth in the standings.

Pablo Larrazábal and Sebastian Soderberg missed the cut and are among those losing DP World Tour status, with Soderberg projected to fall from 101st to 103rd. Kiradech Aphibarnrat withdrew injured, so misses out on Category 10 status. Jason Scrivener, Zander Lombard and Ross Fisher also missed the cut, while Sean Crocker made the weekend and hopes to move into the top 100. Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra shot 66 after an opening 72.
Golf.copy:
Race to Dubai title contender Casey Jarvis holds a share of the halfway lead at the Genesis Championship, with Open champion Ryan Fox also in contention. South African Jarvis, who can move above Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy to second in the season-long standings with a victory, posted a second-round 67 to share top spot with Antoine Rozner at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club.

Jarvis - already a two-time winner on the DP World Tour this season - sits on 10 under with Rozner, who posted a six-under 65, while Champion Golfer of the Year Fox is three strokes back in a share of third.

Golf.summary: Nick Faldo on LIV Golf: "Sport must have consequences" www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
For Nick Faldo, the problem with LIV Golf isn't the money, but what's missing: the fear of failure. In late August, the six-time major champion spoke on the "Sky Sports Golf Podcast" about the future of the league. His reasoning went to the heart of the format. Today, nearly two months later, LIV is in the middle of bankruptcy proceedings, and several stars have left the league.

LIV's season finale provided the occasion for the conversation. The team finale in Michigan had been cancelled, and the tournament in Indianapolis became the final event of the 2026 season. There, rookie Michael La Sasso won with 18 under par, one stroke ahead of Jon Rahm. The 22-year-old became the youngest winner in LIV history.

Golf.title: Race To Dubai Update: Can Casey Jarvis Make It A Four Horse Race?
Golf.summary: Race To Dubai Update: Can Casey Jarvis Make It A Four Horse Race? Golf Monthly
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra's victory at the DP World India Championship took him above Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed to the top of the Race to Dubai rankings. Casey Jarvis, fourth before the Genesis Championship in Korea, led after day one and could climb to third with a top-two finish, or to second with a win.

Points rise sharply in the closing DP World Tour Play-Offs in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, where the title will be decided. McIlroy is chasing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, while Reed would become only the second American winner. Jarvis, 23, won the Magical Kenya Open and South African Open early in the season, and Chacarra, a former LIV Golf player, won the KLM Open and Open d'Italia in June.
Golf.copy:
It was supposed to be a two-horse race between big guns Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed before Eugenio Chacarra's surging form saw him muscle in on the act. But that three-way battle could become a four-strong contest heading into the DP World Tour Play-Offs if Casey Jarvis can back-up a fine start at the Genesis Championship in Korea.

After a couple of near misses, Chacarra's victory at the DP World India Championship saw the Spaniard overtake both McIlroy and Reed to climb to the top of the points rankings.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau Confirms DP World Tour Start But Still 'Committed' To LIV Golf 2.0
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau Confirms DP World Tour Start But Still 'Committed' To LIV Golf 2.0 Golf Monthly
bullets: Bryson DeChambeau has been confirmed for the Nedbank Golf Challenge at Sun City, South Africa, on 3-6 December, where he will face Justin Rose, Marco Penge and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan. It will be his first non-Major DP World Tour start since 2022 and his first competitive action since the LIV Golf finale in August. Gary Player had announced his entry in August.

ESPN has reported that DeChambeau remains committed to LIV Golf and is working to bring LIV Golf 2.0 to life. A 25 October deadline applies for chief executive Scott O'Neil to sign enough players, as a $300m investment from BC Partners depends on the number and quality of signings, although the deadline could be extended. DeChambeau had reportedly spoken to the DP World Tour about more starts next season, but Guy Kinnings has said players must choose one tour or the other.
Golf.copy:
Bryson DeChambeau has confirmed his appearance at December's Nedbank Golf Challenge on the DP World Tour, but he is reportedly still focused on helping LIV Golf 2.0 become a reality.

The two-time US Open champion was announced as an entrant for 'Africa's Major' back in August by Gary Player himself - and now the tournament has confirmed his appearance. The Nedbank Golf Challenge in honour of Gary Player will take place at Sun City from 3-6 December where De Chambeau will take on the likes of Justin Rose, Marco Penge and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan.

Golf.title: Nelly Korda could wrap up LPGA Player of the Year while sitting at home
Golf.summary: Nelly Korda could wrap up LPGA Player of the Year while sitting at home Golfweek
bullets: Nelly Korda could clinch the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award while on a two-month break from the tour. The world No. 1 leads South Korea's Haeran Ryu by 75 points. If the gap exceeds 60 points after the Toto Japan Classic, Korda will clinch mathematically with two events remaining. Ryu would need three wins, or two wins, a second-place and an eighth-place finish, to overtake her.

The award carries one LPGA Hall of Fame point, and Korda, 28, has 25 of the 27 needed for induction. She won four of her first eight events this season, including the first two majors, while Ryu won the next two. Jeeno Thitikul needs three wins and Miyu Yamashita four to overtake Korda. Korda clinched the award with two events left in 2024, and the race has been decided at the CME Group Tour Championship seven times in the last 10 years.
Golf.copy:
- Nelly Korda could win the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award while on a two-month break from the tour. - Korda currently leads her closest competitor, Haeran Ryu, by 75 points in the standings.

- The award is worth one LPGA Hall of Fame point, and Korda is currently two points shy of the 27 needed for induction. - Korda won four of her first eight events this season, including the first two majors.

Golf.title: Louis Oosthuizen the latest to quit LIV for DP World Tour return
Golf.summary: Louis Oosthuizen the latest to quit LIV for DP World Tour return Irish Golfer Magazine
Golf.copy:
On Wednesday, longtime LIV captain and former major champion Louis Oosthuizen announced his departure from LIV Golf, dealing the latest blow to the league’s future. Oosthuizen joins Jon Rahm as the most notable LIV players to publicly confirm their exits from the league. And while Rahm is a far better player than Oosthuizen, and his decision to leave far more impactful, Oosthuizen’s importance to the league should not be overlooked.

He captained the Southern Guards team for LIV’s entire existence. That team was made up entirely of South African pros, and LIV’s South Africa tournament has been one of its biggest success stories. Furthermore, Oosthuizen’s success in major championships, including his 2010 Open Championship victory and a pile of high finishes, raised the stature of the league.

Golf.title: Another major champion set for LIV exit
Golf.summary: Another major champion set for LIV exit Irish Golfer Magazine
bullets: Louis Oosthuizen has said he will not continue in LIV Golf's planned next iteration, becoming the latest major champion set to leave the league. The 2010 Open champion told the South China Morning Post at the Asian Tour's Link Hong Kong Open that the travel schedule would be too demanding for his body at 44, and confirmed his decision in a statement on Instagram.

Oosthuizen joins Jon Rahm, who has ruled himself out of LIV next season, while Sergio Garcia's contract was terminated in the courts, though he could still re-sign. Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed left before the 2026 season, meaning seven major winners had already departed. The league's future remains uncertain despite BC Partners' pledge to invest, and Oosthuizen, who played for Southern Guards GC, said he would prefer to play three weeks at a time in one location.
Golf.copy:
With LIV Golf’s future shrouded in doubt despite BC Partners’ pledge to invest, another major champion has declared himself out of whatever form the league continues in. Jon Rahm has already ruled himself out of being a LIV player next season, and Sergio Garcia has had his contract terminated in the courts though could still re-sign before the start of next season. Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed left before the start of the 2026 season, meaning that a total of seven major championship wins had already made their way to the exit.

And now Louis Oosthuizen looks set to make it eight. The 2010 Open champion is in Hong Kong for the Asian Tour’s Link Hong Kong Open and he told the South China Morning Post that he has no plans to continue playing in LIV 2.0 should it get off the ground as he expects that the travel schedule will be too much for the 44-year-old’s body.

Golf.title: I had one of my best competitive years in 2026. Here's how my gear helped me
Golf.summary: This past year was one of my best competitive seasons, and it came after I made wholesale changes to my golf bag. The post I had one of my best competitive years in 2026. Here’s how my gear helped me appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
This past year, I had perhaps my best competitive season since high school, and a big reason was the new trust I had in my equipment. This season, I shot 71 twice, made an albatross, got my handicap index back below 1.0, and qualified for my first state amateur or mid-amateur in five years. The journey started, though, when we embarked on Fully Fit, a fitting bonanza that gave me the chance to get fit by six OEMs and decide what clubs would make it into my bag for the upcoming year. While I had been GOLF’s gear editor for about a year, I still had yet to take that kind of holistic look at my entire golf bag with each OEM. In fact, at that point, I had had a full bag fitting with just two of them.

It’s not so much that I had any gaping holes in my bag, but there was so much I hadn’t tried. While many of my fittings ended up in product that I would have expected, other spots I tried something new.

Golf.summary: Tom Kim Ends 1,001-Day Wait With Genesis Scottish Open Victory www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
Tom Kim is a PGA Tour winner again. The 24-year-old South Korean shot a bogey-free, 6-under 64 in the final round of the 2026 Genesis Scottish Open on July 12. He finished on 17-under 263 at The Renaissance Club in North Berwick and won by two shots from Min Woo Lee. It was the fourth PGA Tour title of his career and ended a wait of 1,001 days since his last win.

Kim pointed to one early swing on Sunday as the key to his round. On the second hole, playing into the wind, he hit a 2-iron to seven feet. He missed the birdie putt, but the quality of the shot told him something special could happen.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy backs a possible PGA Tour return for select LIV Golf players
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy backs a possible PGA Tour return for select LIV Golf players Yahoo Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on 13 October that he would vote to welcome former LIV Golf players back to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. He argued their return could improve the tours' business prospects and strengthen their fields, while criticising how LIV used its financial resources. He acknowledged that not all players would share his view.

LIV's future is uncertain after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said it would end its funding after the 2026 season and the league entered Chapter 11 proceedings. BC Partners received court approval for up to $300 million in financing, and a decision on LIV 2.0 is expected by the end of October. DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has said players in LIV 2.0 in 2027 cannot compete on the European circuit. The PGA Tour's Returning Member Program, introduced in January 2026, carries a $5 million charitable contribution, and CEO Brian Rolapp said in August there were no plans to revive it.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has signaled a willingness to welcome former LIV Golf players back to the PGA Tour, adding a significant twist to professional golf's ongoing divide. The Northern Irish star, once among the breakaway league's most outspoken critics, now believes bringing certain players back could strengthen the tour commercially and competitively.

His latest comments arrive as LIV Golf confronts serious financial uncertainty and several prominent players reassess their futures. However, McIlroy's support doesn't amount to an unrestricted invitation for every former rival. Questions about eligibility, financial consequences, and the views of current PGA Tour members remain central to any potential reintegration.

Golf.title: How shared stewardship helps drive the game forward
Golf.summary: There's more golf around us than ever. Here's why we need to embrace these additional forms while also creating pathways into more traditional golf. The post How shared stewardship helps drive the game forward appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
This piece was first published on the USGA’s website. In 2009, World Golf Hall of Famer Tom Watson, then 59, was on the verge of becoming the oldest major champion in history. After a nearly perfect iron shot into the 18th green landed firmly and rolled over the putting surface, Tom made bogey and lost in a playoff. Even so, it was an incredible runner-up finish.

Over the years, Tom and my dad, the longtime head golf professional at Delray Dunes Golf & Country Club, forged a strong friendship. Dad wanted to congratulate him on his inspiring performance. Knowing Tom had likely received hundreds of messages, I thought it unlikely we would ever hear back from him following his legendary near-miss.

TGL, the simulator golf league co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, returns this winter for its third season after a successful inaugural campaign that proved the concept and a second season that added new holes, tweaked gameplay and built momentum.

TGL’s third season will see a new team enter the mix, too, as Motor City GC will be the league’s seventh franchise. On Tuesday, TGL announced the complete rosters for its third season, and there have been some changes along with the introduction of Motor City GC. Before, teams had four players on a roster, with three participating each week. Golf.title: Hero World Challenge field announced, but will Tiger Woods play?
Golf.summary: The field for the 2026 Hero World Challenge is mostly set, although there are still spots available if the host, Tiger Woods, wants to play. The post Hero World Challenge field announced, but will Tiger Woods play? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Seven of the world's top 10 players will compete at the Hero World Challenge, hosted by Tiger Woods, at Albany in the Bahamas on 3-6 December. Scottie Scheffler, Matt Fitzpatrick and Cameron Young headline the field. Only 17 of the 20 players were announced on Monday, with three places left as "TBA tournament exemption" spots.

Woods is not yet in the field, but he could take one of the exemptions, as he has done in some previous years. He has not played competitively since missing the cut at the 2024 Open Championship, and he last played the Hero in 2023. He ruptured his Achilles in March 2025 and had a back disc replacement in October 2025. He has also been named on the TGL season three roster, as captain of Jupiter Links.
Golf.copy:
The field for this year’s Hero World Challenge is mostly set, with few surprises, although now the big storyline is if the tournament host will tee it up as well. Seven of the top 10 players in the world will compete at the Tiger Woods-hosted Hero World Challenge Dec. 3-6 at Albany in the Bahamas, and no, Woods is not in the 20-player field. At least not yet.

While it wouldn’t be surprising if Woods sat this one out, only 17 players were announced Monday, with three spots remaining for a “TBA tournament exemption.” Leaving a few spots available for last-minute exemptions is typical for the Hero, and it also makes it convenient for Woods to snag one himself — without kicking a player out — if he’s satisfied with his health and game. In past years Woods has used one of these exemptions on himself, but other times he’s passed on it.

Golf.title: You can now (finally) play this once off-limits Wyoming stunner
Golf.summary: New accommodations at Snake River Sporting Club offer guests a way on to a spectacular Tom Weiskopf design. The post You can now (finally) play this once off-limits Wyoming stunner appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Early in your round at Snake River Sporting Club, you pass a wooden cabin about the size of a turnstand. No snacks are on sale here. It’s only the 3rd hole, you don’t need them yet. The cabin is a relic: evidence that homesteaders were here before Tom Weiskopf, before the club, before any of this was given over to golf.

In the early 1800s, this swath of land alongside the Snake River, south of what is now Jackson Hole, Wyo., was fertile ground for the fur trade. Prospectors of other stripes came later, settling down and building infrastructure of all kinds, including that modest wooden cabin. Another century passed before Weiskopf arrived. The former major champion-turned-course architect drew up a routing that became the centerpiece of an exclusive golf club. The course opened in 2006, making it much younger than the cabin. Like the cabin, though, it fits the landscape. It looks as if it’s been there all along.

Golf.copy:
Your golf bag works harder than almost anything else you own. It hauls 14 clubs (15 if nobody’s looking), dozens of balls, a rangefinder, a rain jacket and whatever snack and drink stash you opt to carry. And it does it every round. If we’re being honest, most of us probably don’t think about our bag until something goes wrong: a zipper that sticks, a strap that digs in, a divider that lets your irons clang together.

Then there’s the summer. Months of heat and direct sun fade fabric, wear down zippers, and weaken stitching. Sweaty hands and wet-weather rounds leave their mark too. Your bag that felt fine in May can be pretty tired by October.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: I hit my ball to the edge of the cup. How long can I wait for it to fall in?
Golf.summary: When your ball ends up on the edge of the cup, how long do you get to wait for it to fall in? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: I hit my ball to the edge of the cup. How long can I wait for it to fall in? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Jack hits his approach to the very edge of the cup, while his playing partners all miss the putting surface. He checks on his ball but doesn’t mark it until the others are on the green, hoping it will fall in during the extended wait. Is this allowed? – Daryl Laumann, via email

By “very edge of the cup,” presumably you mean the ball is overhanging the edge. In this case, Jack gets a reasonable time to reach the ball, from however far away that might be, and then 10 seconds maximum to see if it will fall in — whether the other players have reached the green or not. (Clarification 13.3a/1 highlights the meaning of “reasonable time.”)

Golf.title: 2 huge reasons golfers have early extension — and how to fix them
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Brian Mogg explains two reasons he sees golfers early extend — and shares how to fix them. The post 2 huge reasons golfers have early extension — and how to fix them appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
One of the most common swing problems I see among recreational golfers is early extension. You’ve probably heard the term before. It occurs when your hips and pelvis move toward the golf ball during the downswing, leaving less room for your arms and club to move freely through impact. The result? Your chest rises, your posture changes, and making consistent contact becomes much more difficult.

But here’s something I’ve learned after decades of teaching golfers around the world: Early extension is often the result of another swing flaw, not the original problem. That’s why simply telling a golfer to keep their hips back doesn’t always work. To make a lasting improvement, you need to understand what’s causing your hips to move toward the ball in the first place.

We stayed on the north coast at Puerto Plata and played Playa Dorada, a Robert Trent Jones course that opened in 1976.

Expecting to get a couple of rounds in, I think we played seven or eight times and a love affair with golf in the Caribbean was born. I've not been back to Playa Dorada, but I remember it with great affection.

Golf.title: As LIV Golf fades away, Eugenio Chacarra might be the biggest winner of golf's civil war
Golf.summary: Just about everyone in pro golf benefitted from the the PGA Tour-LIV battle. But perhaps no one was a bigger winner than Eugenio Chacarra. The post As LIV Golf fades away, Eugenio Chacarra might be the biggest winner of golf’s civil war appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra, 26, took the Race to Dubai lead by winning the DP World India Championship with rounds of 67-67-63-70, beating Daniel Hillier by two for his third title of the season. The Spaniard left LIV Golf after the 2024 season having earned $16 million in 34 starts, and has since won the Hero Indian Open, KLM Open and DS Automobiles 83° Open d'Italia.

Chacarra said he wanted major starts, Ryder Cups and DP World Tour wins, and that LIV had given him a financial base and a strong team. He improved his nutrition and recovery in 2026 and played through a fractured toe, finishing T3 at the French Open and T2 at the Spanish Open. His results have all but secured his 2027 PGA Tour spot, while LIV is in bankruptcy court.
Golf.copy:
If you ask Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose, or any number of top pros, almost everyone benefited from the years-long battle between the PGA Tour, the DP World Tour, and LIV Golf. If you stuck with the established tours, LIV’s emergence forced them to make needed changes; purses increased and stagnation ended. If you defected to the then-Saudi-backed league, you secured riches that were exponentially greater than what pro golfers had thought possible. Some, like Bryson DeChambeau, increased their popularity. Some, like Lee Westwood and Ian Poulter, got a nice payday as their careers reached the final stage. Others, like Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed, got in early and left before the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew funding, sending LIV into a tailspin that has landed the league in bankruptcy court, where it is sinking as players exit. Time will tell how much the defection cost players like Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith when it comes to major opportunities and overall legacy, but they still benefited greatly from the move and will likely get to return to the tour whose shores they once torched in due time.

But while most of pro golf’s many stakeholders finished the civil war in the green, perhaps no one was a bigger winner than Eugenio Chacarra. The young Spaniard was one of the first to leave for LIV Golf. He was the No. 2-ranked amateur in the world while at Oklahoma State and elected to take a signing bonus to join Sergio Garcia’s Fireballs GC team in 2022 instead of pursuing his initial dream: the PGA Tour. Chacarra, a ball-striking star, won early on LIV but then struggled with injuries. His contract wasn’t renewed after the 2024 season, and he chose not to try to earn his spot back on the rebel tour via LIV Q School. Instead, Chacarra aired his grievances about how things were done on LIV. He said it was about “only money” and he wanted more. After earning $16 million in 34 starts on LIV, Chacarra wanted to chase his original dreams and believed his game could get him there in due time.

Golf.title: 'How would he know?': Rory McIlroy dismisses Kevin Kisner's cash-grab claim
Golf.summary: At the DP World India Championship, Rory McIlroy dismissed Kevin Kisner's suggestion that he had made the trip just for the money. The post ‘How would he know?’: Rory McIlroy dismisses Kevin Kisner’s cash-grab claim appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy responded to Kevin Kisner's claim that he played the DP World India Championship in New Delhi purely for money, asking "How would he know that?" McIlroy, who was in the event for a second straight year, received an undisclosed appearance fee, as did other leading players including Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose.

Kisner, speaking on the Fore Play podcast, said many players are paid to appear and doubted that the aim was to expand golf in India. McIlroy said both could be true, noting that players can be paid while genuinely trying to bring the sport to a developing country where the middle class exceeds the population of the United States. He finished T42, 17 shots behind winner Eugenio Chacarra.
Golf.copy:
Just because Rory McIlroy is growing his bank account doesn’t mean he isn’t also trying to grow the game. So the Northern Irishman said in response to criticism from Kevin Kisner, who questioned McIlroy’s stated motivations for playing in this week’s DP World India Championship in New Delhi.

In case you missed it, here’s the context. McIlroy was in the tournament for the second straight year and, like several other marquee players in the field, including Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose, he received an undisclosed appearance fee.

Golf.title: How the PGA Tour's best putter warms up before every round
Golf.summary: Get an in-depth look at Jacob Bridgeman's practice putting routine and steal his keys to boost your performance on the green. The post How the PGA Tour’s best putter warms up before every round appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Jacob Bridgeman led the PGA Tour this season with 63.585 total Strokes Gained: Putting, more than 23 strokes clear of the next-best player on 40.43. He keeps his approach simple, avoiding tinkering with his stroke and concentrating on start line, distance control and building consistency from close range.

In a video with TaylorMade, he explained that his warm-up begins with a start-line drill, using tees as a gate over a four- to six-foot, slightly uphill putt. He then works around the hole from four to six feet, before moving to seven-and-a-half and nine feet and varying pace with three balls. He finishes with 15 minutes of realistic scenarios, saying: "The less I do, the less can go wrong."
Golf.copy:
Jacob Bridgeman is on a roll with his putter, and the numbers are pretty wild. This season, he led the field with 63.585 total Strokes Gained: Putting, more than 23 strokes ahead of the next-best player at 40.43. In other words, his putter gives him a serious advantage over his competitors.

So, what’s the secret to his success on the greens? Surprisingly, Bridgeman keeps things pretty simple. He doesn’t tinker with his stroke or get caught up in the mechanics. Instead, he focuses on his start line, distance control and building his consistency from close range.

Golf.title: What these former NHL stars think about their golf games | Subpar
Golf.summary: On GOLF's Subpar podcast, former NHLers Brenden Morror and Mike Commodore talked hockey fights, golf matches and more. The post What these former NHL stars think about their golf games | Subpar appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
If there’s anything better than being a professional athlete, it’s being a retired professional athlete who’s really good at golf. You get to extend your competitive career, only now the stakes are a little lower and the equipment is a lot different.

Brenden Morrow has taken that route, competing on The Pro Tour, an invitation-only circuit for retired professional athletes. His fellow former NHLer, Mike Commodore, can get around a golf course, too, though he’s not quite convinced his game is ready for The Pro Tour.

Golf.title: Japanese Pro Secures Masters And Open Spots With Victory At National Championship
Golf.summary: Yusaku Hosono's second victory of the season has earned him invitations to two of golf's biggest events
bullets: Yusaku Hosono won the Japan Open Golf Championship at Tarao Country Club by two shots over Yusuke Sakamoto, earning places at the 2027 Masters and Open Championship. He shot rounds of 65, 64, 68 and 70, and it was his second win of the season after the Japan PGA Championship Senko Group Cup in May.

Invitations come through an alignment between Augusta National and The R&A that began in 2025 and was confirmed in September to continue. Hosono is the third player to qualify for both Majors this way, after Tom Kim via the Genesis Scottish Open and Grant Forrest via the Open de Espana. Winners of the Hong Kong Open, Australian Open and South African Open will also receive invitations. The 2027 Open is at the Old Course, St Andrews.
Golf.copy:
Yusaku Hosono has booked his place at next year's Masters and Open Championship after securing a two-shot victory at the Japan Open Golf Championship in his homeland. Hosono’s win at Tarao Country Club was his second of an impressive season after victory at the Japan PGA Championship Senko Group Cup in May.

However, with invitations to two of golf's biggest events also secured, his win in his home open is the more significant of the two. In September, Augusta National Golf Club and The R&A confirmed that an alignment that began in 2025, which would see invites to The Masters and The Open given to winners of select opens, would continue.

Golf.title: Chacarra wins in India to take Race to Dubai lead
Golf.summary: Eugenio Chacarra wins the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club by two strokes, finishing on 21 under to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy. After rounds of 67 and 67, bad light halted his third round on Saturday; he completed a nine-under 63 on Sunday for a five-shot lead, then shot 70 to hold off New Zealand's Daniel Hillier, who birdied the last.

It was the 26-year-old Spaniard's third win of the season, and he aims to become the third Spaniard to top the standings after Jon Rahm and Seve Ballesteros. Reed, who had led since March, finished eight under in a tie for 23rd, while McIlroy shot 74 in the final round to share 42nd. Three events remain before the winner is crowned next month.
Golf.copy:
Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy. Spain's Chacarra finished on 21 under, with American Reed and world number two McIlroy well off the pace by the final round of this event.

After opening with successive scores of 67 in his first two rounds at Delhi Golf Club, bad light halted play with Chacarra still on the 11th hole of his third round on Saturday.

Golf.title: 'How Would He Know That?'
Golf.summary: The six-time Major winner has responded to Kisner's suggestion that his main motivation for playing in the DP World India Championship was his appearance fee
bullets: Rory McIlroy has rejected Kevin Kisner's claim that he played the DP World India Championship only for a large appearance fee. Kisner told the Fore Play podcast that McIlroy "wants to get his $10m and go play in India". McIlroy, who finished tied for 42nd at Delhi Golf Club, replied: "How would he know that?"

McIlroy said two things can be true at once: players can be paid to appear while also having a genuine interest in growing golf in India, where the middle class is larger than the whole US population. He called India an important market for golf. He is third in the Race to Dubai behind Eugenio Chacarra and Patrick Reed, and said Chacarra's form makes his bid for an eighth title harder with two events left.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has responded to Kevin Kisner’s claim that he only played in the DP World India Championship because he received a large appearance fee. Kisner gave his opinion on McIlroy’s reason for playing at the Delhi Golf Club event to the Fore Play podcast.

He poured scorn on the six-time Major winner's supposed motivation for playing, which he suggested was to help grow the game globally. He said: "That is such a dog s*** comment. But I guess for the right price we could all say that.
